question_name: Describe any planned climate-related projects within your jurisdiction for which you hope to attract financing.
column_name: Project description and attach project proposal
response_answer: Under this action, Lagos State will undertake an evaluation of the cur- rent status of waste management and develop a Waste Infrastructure Development Strategy by 2022. The evaluation will be based on data on tons of waste collected, waste composition and volumes processed by MRF and composting facilities. The strategy will aim to increase the capacity of Lagos’s waste transfer, material recovery, bio- digester and composting facilities. It will mandate the construction of new waste infrastructure, including transfer loading stations, starting in Iberekodo, Agunlejika and Odogunyan. The strat- egy will build on the progress the State has made so far in establishing waste transfer stations and expanding the waste vehicle fleet. The new facilities will need to have the capacity to absorb the expected increase in the volume of recyclables diverted from landfill due to the launch of the Lagos Recycling Initiative. Implementation of the strat- egy is expected to require State funding and cooperation with the private sector through PPPs. The State could institute a levy on waste disposal to support infrastructure investments. A number of previous projects were abandoned because their operation was deemed unfeasible; demand must be confirmed in the planning phase and consideration must be given to how these projects can be made sustainable in the long term. For wastewater management, the State Government intends to develop an Outline Business Case (OBC) study and WIDP for the sector. The OBC study/ WIDP will cover the preparation of detailed engineering designs, drawings and specifications, construction and operational cost estimates, environ- mental and social impact assessments, and analysis of required land use for wastewater infrastructure provision for existing and projected population of the State, in line with Regional Masterplan of the State. The WIDP will further determine project implementation and phasing plan, set timelines and process to be followed for project procurement (either through government funding or through private sector participation), while the OBC study will specifically provide a well-developed and compre- hensive suite of project documents that will be made available to private inves- tors during the procurement process. This is a useful tool that will bring all the elements of the project together, so that any conflicts between factors can be resolved before approaching the pri- vate sector. This document will be used to form the basis on which the project will be assessed and approved for com- mencement of the procurement phase. It will also have served as an investment document to engender the interest of investors and facilitate the implemen- tation of wastewater treatment projects through public private partnerships (PPP) procurement routes. In addition to this, all existing wastewater treat- ment infrastructure in the State will be upgraded and expanded to cover more catchment areas, these include Alausa wastewater treatment plant (WWTP), Abesan WWTP, Oke-Afa WWTP and Iponri WWTP.

response_answer: The State government is aware there is an energy deficit however some areas such as snake island can only be accessed via a ferry thus when issues arise like these, they can only rely on renewable energy. There has been no substantive study to access the energy poverty for the city however a study has been done on Lagos Informal Settlement Household Energy Survey to  assess the various fuel types and energy uses by residential settlements in informal settlements.The aim of the survey is to addresss the gaps in the available city data on energy consumption patterns from cooking and electricity /lighting in informal settlements.

question_name: Provide information on your jurisdiction’s oversight of climate-related risks and opportunities and how these issues have impacted your jurisdiction's planning.
column_name: Describe the risks to your jurisdiction related to the transition to a low-carbon economy
response_answer: The economy of the country is still largely dependent on fossil fuels being an oil-producing country however gradually we are witnessing the transition to renewable energy as there is increasing uptake of solar photovoltaics technology in homes and also in government institutions, particularly the Primary Health Care facilities are being considered for off-grid power supply due to the vaccines that are required to be at optimal temperatures. The increasing uptake of solar photovoltaic technology is leading to the creation of new jobs such as installers, technicians and maintenance persons whose skills will be required regularly. However, there is still a skills gap to meet the growing demand for PV technology.  Other risks include the financing risk of transitioning to a low-carbon economy and slow adoption of technology have also proven to be hindrances to the transition to a low-carbon economy.Also, in the waste management sector, the city is witnessing more people being involved in waste segregation and acting in the capacity of aggregators and middlemen for livelihood. Behavioural patterns also pose a risk to the adoption of a circular economy so there are still challenges for city-wide adoption of source segregation of waste.

This council consists of Honourable Commissioners from relevant Government Ministries. Additionally, a Technical Committee has been established, which includes representatives from various Ministries, Departments, Government Agencies, State Supported Research Institutions, and reputable Non-Governmental Organizations. The Honourable Commissioner for Environment & Water Resources oversees this Technical Committee.To facilitate the operations of the State Council on Climate Change, the Climate Change and Environmental Planning Department serves as the Secretariat. The government is actively committed to collaborating with all relevant stakeholders to effectively tackle climate change challenges and build a resilient and strong system.

response_answer: Yes , Based on the 2015 baseline inventory, in combination with population and economic growth forecasts, the inventory team developed an emissions growth projection up to 2050. This emissions pathway was termed the business-as-usual (BAU) scenario. and the modelling was undertaken using the Pathways Scenario Planning Tool.The BAU scenario indicates that if no climate actions are undertaken, Lagos’s emissions will triple by 2050. This scenario models activity and emissions growth without action or policy. Lagos' targets for emission reduction relative to the Business-as-Usual scenario were presented showing that in order to achieve the proposed emission reduction targets, this will require ambitious action in all sectors.

Developing diverse energy sources: Taipei City is committed to promoting the development and utilization of diverse energy sources, including renewable energy, to reduce reliance on fossil fuels.3. Enhancing public transportation: Taipei City prioritizes the development and improvement of its public transportation system, including the expansion of the metro network, the promotion of bus rapid transit (BRT) systems, and the implementation of bike-sharing programs. These efforts aim to provide convenient and sustainable transportation options, reducing the reliance on private vehicles.2. response_answer: Taipei City Promotion Taskforce of Flood Resilient-Resistant Community Projecthttps://heo.gov.taipei/cp.aspx?n=0FB7DE550257C53CIn 2019, the “Taipei City Promotion Taskforce of Flood Resilient-Resistant Community Project” was initiated. A professional consultant team was entrusted to handle the advocacy and the promotion of disaster-resistant matters in the communities and on campuses. In 2019, we promoted communities located in the Dahu Village in Neihu District, Jiangshan Village in Zhongshan District, and Guangneng Village in Datong District. When the heavy rain occurs, residents are quickly gathered for evacuation, rescue, and other emergency responses, and after the heavy rain stops, post-disaster recovery is carried out, such as cutting down the collapsed trees on the road, assisting the evacuation of disadvantaged groups, CPR and AED performance, flood gate operations, and water pump operations.In addition, Taipei City Government Hydraulic Engineering Office of the Public Works Department also refers to the analysis of flooding potential and the water accumulation events over the years before the flood period every year. response_answer: Taipei City established the “Council for Sustainable Development of Taipei City Government” in 2004. The Council is composed of government officials, experts and scholars, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), and business representatives. It is divided into 7 major task groups including the Sustainability Vision Group, Water and Land Resources Group, Energy and Ecology Group, Sustainable Transportation Group, Sustainable Community Group, Sustainable Education Group, and Livable Environment Group. The Council holds quarterly committee meetings to make period adjustments and conduct reviews of sustainable development matters such as greenhouse gas mitigation and adaptation. In addition, we abide by the provisions of Taiwan's “Greenhouse Gas Reduction and Management Act” and develop carbon reduction promotion measures based on regional emission characteristics and reduction targets. In 2019, the City also formulated the “Taipei City Greenhouse Gas Control Action Plan,” and established the “greenhouse gas supervision and reporting.” The mayor serves as the convener to supervise the implementation of the energy-saving and carbon-reduction action plan by the relevant agencies of the City government's four major departments (residential and commercial, transportation, waste, agriculture and forestry) on a quarterly basis. The City invite experts and scholars to jointly discuss how to strengthen the implementation effectiveness and achieve the City's carbon reduction goals of every 5 year.The City connects with the globe and leads the country to announce that it will achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 on April 22, 2021. The City proposed a net-zero emissions pathway, and to implement and achieve the net-zero emissions goal, it has integrated the regulatory organizations mentioned above and incorporated it into the “Energy Conservation Promotion Task Force” and other diversified and deep carbon reduction organizations. In cooperation with Taiwan’s “Climate Change Response Act”, the City transformed the “Council for Sustainable Development of Taipei City Government” into the “Climate Change Response Promotional Committee.” The mayor serve as the convener, and the city's “Greenhouse Gas Reduction Implementation Plan” and “Climate Change Adaptation Implementation Plan” will be reviewed by the Promotional Committee and submitted to the central government for approval and promulgation. In addition to actively promoting mitigation and adaptation and other climate actions and policies, the Government will compile reports on the results of the 2 implementation plans mentioned before and will be made public each year.To promote the city's net-zero transition, the City proposed the “Taipei City Self-Government Ordinance for Net-Zero Emissions”, which, in addition to writing the city's goals for net-zero emissions into law, the ordinance will specify the authority and responsibilities of each department of the government, introduce the carbon budget system, and establish climate transformation fund (special funds are dedicated to climate change adaptation, greenhouse gas reduction, taking care of the disadvantaged during climate transition, and ensuring a just transition). To strengthen climate resilience, a special chapter on adaptation has been written. In addition, the city's three net-zero pathways, including smart and zero-carbon buildings, green and low-carbon transportation, and complete cycle zero-waste will be promoted, as well as the incremental exchange of new development projects, installation of renewable energy by large energy consumers, development of electric/hydrogen vehicles, reduction or prohibition the use of disposable products, environmentally friendly container recycling systems and other zero-carbon life promotion measures.

response_answer: In order to promote the use of green transportation in Taipei City, the framework is centered around the Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) system as the backbone, supplemented by buses, and encourages walking or cycling for first and last-mile journeys. The city government will continue to implement various push-pull policies to enhance the convenience and comfort of public transportation. These policies will complement each other to achieve the goal of a 70% green transportation usage rate by 2030, 75% by 2040, and 80% by 2050.1. MRT: 152.3 km of the MRT lines has been opened to traffic in Taipei City. Together with the Xinyi Line East Extension, Wanda-Zhonghe-Shulin Line, and the Northern and Southern sections of the Circular Line, which are currently under construction, and the Eastern section of the Circular Line under planning, the goal is to complete the Capital MRT Circular Line by 2030. The joint construction of the Greater Taipei MRT network will effectively increase the utilization rate of green transportation for the people in both Taipei City and New Taipei City. In 2050, the MRT network will continue to be expanded in line with the development of the Shiodong MRT and Shezidao.2. Buses: By 2030, 100% of the buses will be electrified, and the "MRT-like" concept of the "eight-horizontal and eight-vertical trunk bus network" will be promoted, with a high frequency and a fastest 4-minute headway at peak hours. With the MRT transfer discount, it effectively changes people's transportation habits and increases the proportion of rides.3. Shared vehicles: Taipei City takes resource sharing as the starting point and actively promotes the "4U" project, integrating YouBike, U-Motor, U-Car, and U-Parking services to properly utilize idle equipment and venues (including parking space sharing, vehicle sharing, and ride-sharing). In 2022, there were 14,088 shared motorcycles and 1,450 shared cars in the City.4. Public bicycles: The urban bicycle transportation policy involves transportation, leisure, public construction, and urban operation. With the gradual shift of private transportation to mass transit, road space should return to "humanity-oriented transportation". The City is actively planning a complete road network for bicycles and pedestrians, with a total of 543 km and 13,240 vehicles by 2030, 596 km and 16,000 vehicles by 2040, and 21,500 vehicles by 2050.

response_answer: Solar Photovoltaic:1. Before 2015, the solar photovoltaic power generation equipment was set up by all government departments and schools according to their own budgets, the investment was NT$450 million, and 2,140kW were installed. In 2016, the "Regulation of Governing Provision of Solar Photovoltaic Power Generation Equipment onto the Use of Public Premises in Taipei City" was promulgated and implemented. Through the bidding of the City’s government departments and schools' municipal properties, the properties are for enterprises to build photovoltaic systems. The government has made zero investment, and the City’s solar photovoltaic power generation capacity is gradually expanded through public-private cooperation.2. Ground-mounted photovoltaic: Taipei Energy Hill is a ground-mounted photovoltaic system built through public-private partnerships with land provided by the Taipei City Government and funded by the manufacturers. Under such a system, the Government has made zero investment while the manufacturers bear all the construction costs. In 2017, a landfill site was used to set up the Taipei Energy Hill 1.0, with an installed capacity of about 2MW, generating about 2 million kWh of electricity annually. In 2019, we also used the landfill site to set up the Taipei Energy Hill 2.0, with an installed capacity of about 1MW and generating about 1 million kWh of electricity annually. As of 2021, Taipei Energy Hill 1.0 generated 10.65 million kWh, and Taipei Energy Hill 2.0 generated 2.952 million kWh. Taipei Energy Hill is the pioneering project that installs photovoltaic systems at landfills located countrywide. With the existing biogas generation systems, the landfills can be transformed into green energy and environmental protection parks with the benefit of land revitalization.3. Roof photovoltaic: In 2016, the bidding of the City’s government departments and schools' municipal properties in the north and south districts was completed. As of 2020, the solar roof photovoltaics were set up at a total of 24 locations in the north and south districts, with a total capacity of 4,065 kWh, generating about 4 million kWh of electricity annually. In 2020, the roof photovoltaics were set up in 34 schools, with a total capacity of about 5,499 kWh, generating about 5.24 million kWh of electricity annually. The MRT Corporation has installed photovoltaics with an installed capacity of about 3,797 kWh in the MRT Beitou depot, and the annual power generation is estimated to be up to 4 million kWh. The Taipei Water Department Changxing Water Purification Plant is the first water purification plant in Taiwan to fully cover the top of the plant with electricity. It has an installed capacity of about 2,137 kWh, and the maximum power generation is estimated to be 2.13 million kWh.4. To assist citizens in participating in the utilization of renewable energy, the City provides consultation and matching on the installation of photovoltaics. In December 2020, the largest civil power plant in Taiwan was set up in Guandu Junior High School. The estimated annual power generation of the project is about 19,000 kWh, and the annual carbon reduction is about 10.46 metric tons, which is equivalent to planting 955 trees 1% of the revenue generated from the electricity goes to the city government, and 2% goes to Guandu Junior High School to promote environmental education. In 2021, bids in 5 locations were completed. The installation is expected to be completed in August 2022, with a total of 6 civil power plants.5. As of the end of 2021, there are 72 institutions and 106 schools in this City, with a total of 178 photovoltaics totaling 27,800kWh. The central and private units totaling 41,248kWh, the estimated annual power generation is about 39.35 million kWh, and the carbon reduction is about 19,753 metric tons, which is equivalent to appropriately 50 Daan Forest Parks. The installed capacity and power generation of photovoltaic generation equipment have increased by 22.64% compared with 2020.Hydro power:In 1986, the Feitsui Hydroelectric Power Plant with an installed capacity of 70,000kWh was completed, with an average annual power generation of about 220 million kWh (it can supply about 63,000 households with electricity for one year). By generating power using green hydro power, about 110,000 metric tons of carbon dioxide can be reduced.To sum up, the City's overall renewable energy generation capacity increased by 7.35% in 2021.

response_answer: In 2016, the "Measures for the Use of Solar Photovoltaic Power Generation Equipment Provided by Public Housing Land in Taipei City" was issued and implemented , and used to set up a solar photovoltaic power generation system in combination with private investment.In terms of ground-based photovoltaic power, Taipei City is promoting the "Taipei Energy Hill" project in the Fudekeng Environmental Restoration Park, which is the first landfill photovoltaic power plant in the country to be completed for power generation. The City will provide the land and the vendor will finance the construction and maintenance of the photovoltaic power systems through public tenders. The project occupies about 3 hectares of land and has an installed capacity of 1,996.8 kilo-watts. The installation was completed in December 2016, and the system was launched on January 10, 2017, with a capacity of about 2.08 million kWh and a reduction of about 1,100 metric tons of CO2 emissions. The second phase of the "Taipei Energy Hill" was tendered in 2018 and opened in 2019 with installation of a photovoltaic power systems in Shanshuilu Eco Park in Nangang. The capacity of the system is 980.88 kilo-watts, and the annual power generation is estimated to be 1 million kWh, which can reduce about 550 tons of carbon dioxide emissions per year. In the future, the park will be further planned to become a green energy environmental protection park with multiple functions of environmental education, ecological and environmental protection, recreation, and leisure.Regarding rooftop photovoltaic power, the tender for the northern and southern areas of the municipal public housing for the City's public agencies and schools was completed in 2016. In 2021, the City's Department of Economic Development, Department of Education, Department of Environmental Protection, Public Transportation Office, and Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation invited tenders for the installation of photovoltaic power generation equipment. question_name: Provide details of your emissions reduction target(s). Please report both long-term and mid-term targets, if applicable.
response_answer: Aims to meet a 1.5°C modelled domestic pathway, Taipei City will increase its carbon reduction target from 30% by 2030 compared to 40 % by 2005. In May 2021 , the International Energy Agency (IEA) published "Net Zero by 2050: A Roadmap for the Global Energy Sector", which pointed out that the reduction before 2030 will come from the current large-scale deployment of commercial carbon reduction technologies, and after 2030 reduction will come from the current demonstration or prototype technology applications. In view of this, 2030 will be an important milestone towards 2050 net zero emissions. Taipei City is continuing to work on greenhouse gas reduction and promote climate action under the framework of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). According to the City's 2050 Net Zero Pathway, climate actions and strategies will be implemented through the residential and commercial sectors, as well as transportation and waste.1. Residential and commercial sectors: By 2030, the City will achieve an energy efficiency inventory, disclosure and control of new buildings and public buildings, and new buildings will be required to meet Class 1 energy efficiency standards. The City will also demonstrate zero-carbon building lifecycle design through TOD/EOD, social housing, public construction, introduce hydrogen fuel cell application demonstrations, and implement a total volume control and trading system with reference to Tokyo, Japan.2. Transportation sector: The proportion of green transportation will reach 70% by 2030, the metropolitan MRT loop will be completed, 100% of urban buses will be electrified, electric motorcycles will account for 35% of new vehicles sold, and 24,400 shared vehicles will be actively promoted, while the number of public bicycles will be expanded to 13,240, and the total length of bicycle lanes will reach 543 km. The City will also accelerate the installation of 2,000 charging spaces, 576 smart signal intersections, and will become an air quality maintenance zone.3. Waste sector: The resource recovery rate will reach 70% by 2030. In order to achieve the goal of waste reduction and recycling, disposable tableware and plastic will be banned and recycling containers will be built. In addition, the City will continue to increase the proportion of proper sewage treatment. In addition to planning the construction of water resource regeneration centers and sewerage connection projects, the proportion of the sewage treatment population will reach 94%. Green energy power plants transformed from a waste incinerator will be launched, and waste treatment facilities are gradually planned and will be coordinated to be transformed into a green energy recycling park.

For the realization of an “advanced energy-saving city”, Taipei City is active in promoting and establishing photovoltaic power equipment, and improving the growth rate of renewable energy and creating the sustainable development of energy through the planning and establishment of solar energy at public facilities, venues, and open spaces.Photovoltaic power:1. The budget for photovoltaic power generation equipment was appropriated by the subordinate agencies and schools in Taipei City before 2015 with a total expense of NT$450 million incurred and 2,140 kilowatts generated. The “Regulation of Governing Provisions of Solar Photovoltaic Power Generation Equipment onto the Use of Public Premises in Taipei City” was announced in 2016 to have public premises, including subordinate agencies and schools, leased to enterprises through tenders for the construction of photovoltaic power systems and the photovoltaic power generation capacity of the city will be gradually expanded.2. Ground photovoltaic power: “Taipei Energy Hill” is a ground photovoltaic system constructed through the cooperation of public-private sectors with land provided by the city and funded by the manufacturers.  As of 2022, “Taipei Energy Hill 1.0” generated 12.1 million kWh, and “Taipei Energy Hill 2.0” generated 5.7 million kWh.3. Roof photovoltaic power: The tender for the public premises of the subordinate agencies and schools in the northern and southern districts of the city was completed in 2016. There were a total of 24 locations set up in the northern and southern districts of the city by the year of 2020. There were a total of 34 locations set up in schools by the year of 2020. MRT Corporation has installed a photovoltaic power device with a capacity of about 3,797 kilowatts Beitou Depot. Changxing Purification Plant of Taipei Water Department is the first water purification plant in Taiwan with a solar roof farm constructed for a capacity of 2,137 kilowatts.4. In order to assist residents participating in renewable energy utilization, Taipei City Government provides consultation and matchmaking on the installation of solar panels. The largest citizen power plant in Taiwan was set up in Guan Du Junior High School in December 2020 with an estimated power generation of 19,000 kWh and annual carbon reduction of 10.46 metric tons. One percent (1%) of the income from power generation will be fed back to Taipei City Government and 2% will be fed back to Guan Du Junior High School to promote environmental education. A tender for 5 locations was awarded in 2021 with the construction to be completed in August 2022, a total of 6 citizen power plants cumulatively.5. There were 72 subordinate agencies and 106 schools of Taipei City Government completed by the end of 2021. Also, a total of 41,248 kilowatts was completed by the central government and private sectors, including carbon reduction of 19,753 metric tons. Also, both the photovoltaic power generation equipment capacity and power generation had been increased by 22.64% from the year of 2020.Hydro power:Feitsui Hydro Power Plant was constructed in 1986 and has an output capacity of 70,000 kilowatts with an average annual power generation capacity of about 220 million kWh (sufficient for the annual use of 63,000 households). It uses a hydro-green power generation approach adopted to reduce 110,000 metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions.

response_answer: In response to the extreme climate and heat island effect, Taipei City Government promotes the sponge city, which allows rainwater to infiltrate into the soil through water permeable pavement, increasing the water retention of the base and keeping groundwater. In sunny days, the water kept in the soil can be evaporated to the atmosphere through the water permeable pavement, lowering the surface temperature and regulating the microclimate of the urban environment to achieve the function of reducing the urban heat island effect.The main purpose of water permeable pavement is not to improve waterlogging. For the improvement of flooded areas in Taipei City, the Hydraulic Engineering Office of the Public Works Bureau has added temporary pumping units for low-lying areas to speed up drainage, and has also started improvement works for areas with large differences in the height of the terrain, resulting in faster runoff and ineffective drainage. In addition, during typhoons and rainstorms, the Hydraulic Engineering Office of the Public Works Bureau will mobilize leased machinery and pumping teams to stand by for pumping and draining to reduce the chance of flooding.

response_answer: https://heo.gov.taipei/News_Content.aspx?n=1FE45A3FEA3D194E&sms=72544237BBE4C5F6&s=0F31D02695B2B164The Taipei City Government encourages the citizens to participate in the water environment patrol plan, the operation and maintenance of artificial wetlands, and the removal of flotsam on the river surface, together with the residents near the river, the network of monitoring the river environment is formed. The water environment education and advocacy activities are carried out, provoking the citizen's sense of identity with the land, and spreading the concept of environmental protection to everyone. Through the input of river patrol volunteers, the occurrence of pollution can be effectively prevented or reduced, and the protection of the river environment can be achieved. 1. Combining community organizations, community colleges, village offices, and schools. The City's water environment patrol team is formed to create a force of autonomous river protection by the people.2. In 2021, the Taipei City Water Environment Patrol Team consists of 23 teams with 634 people. The patrol energy of each team is integrated to organize advocacy activities such as stream cleanup, special education and training for volunteers, and encourage community residents and schools to participate in water environment patrol and water quality monitoring activities.3. In 2021, the water environment patrol team conducted 1,336 inspections, 604 simple water quality tests, and 8 stream cleanup activities, removing a total of 389.4 kilograms of garbage.4. Maintain the normal operation of artificial wetlands through operation and maintenance, with an average daily influx of 2,172 m3 to provide fresh water for wetlands in the natural parks, and organize 31 wetland environmental education and promotion activities to promote the sustainable operation of Guandu Nature Park.5. Conduct wetland operation and maintenance, water quality and flow monitoring, ecological survey for birds, and wetland environmental education and promotion.6. To maintain the cleanliness of the river surface and reduce the garbage flowing into the water, we organized the removal of flotsam on the river surface of the Tamsui River, Keelung River, Xindian River, and low-water embankment. We used both mechanical sewage treatment boats and manual removal to clean garbage on the river surface and carried out dredging operations in front of the water pumping station and around the gate valve. In 2021, a total of 4,169.2 metric tons of flotsam on the river surface is removed, reducing the garbage in water.

column_name: Describe the wider opportunities/benefits of climate action the jurisdiction has identified
response_answer: Taipei City has set goals of reducing carbon emissions by 40% by 2030 and achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 based on the current urban development pattern, greenhouse gas emission characteristics, and planned climate actions and goals. Through diversified carbon reduction strategies and measures, the City expands the development of green industries:1. Development of Cleaning Technology Industries: Promote the improvement of energy-saving in the public and private sectors, and promote the replacement of energy-saving equipment in the private sector in various ways, including incentives, subsidies, and counseling. At the same time, we also indirectly encourage the development of ESCO, such as promoting the improvement of energy-saving in the community and the public sector by introducing the ESCO model.2. Improve water safety environment (sponge city): Continue to improve the quality of river water and water environment, properly carry out disaster prevention, flood adaptation, and river dredging work to avoid flooding due to drainage failure caused by extreme rainfall. By 2030, the percentage of green infrastructure (GI) will be 80%, and the tolerance of rainfall intensity will be increased to 88.8mm /hr, and the percentage of recycled water production will be 16%.3. Development of low-carbon sustainable transportation: In addition to the continuous construction of the MRT road network and the optimization of the bus network, the promotion of subsidies for the replacement of vehicles for electric scooters and electric buses is strengthened. The City expects that urban buses will be fully electrified by 2030, and 35% of new scooters sold will be electric.4. Energy Efficiency Measures and Project Development:(1) From 2018 to 2020, through the "Taipei City Residential and Commercial Electricity Saving Action Plan", the replacement of air-conditioning has been prioritized for primary and junior schools, then for the replacement of energy-consuming equipment in residential buildings and service industries. The planning of the outstanding results will be continued, and the “Residential and Commercial Electricity Saving 2.0” plan will be launched successively.(2) The City continues to conduct smart grid constructions to demonstrate how renewable energy and smart power management systems can apply in the metropolitan area for multiple purposes.(3) The incineration plants continue to undergo refurbishment and renovation projects and upgraded/optimized exhaust gas treatment equipment, which reduces dioxin emissions by half, increasing particulate removal rate to 99%, with waste heat utilization equipment being renovated; promote the renewal of operating components of the Feitsui Reservoir’s electric power plant to enhance power generation efficiency.5. Promote a circular economy model:(1) To promote the circular economy in the City, we have set out the "Circular Taipei Strategy Roadmap 2.0" to further develop the "urban resource circular chain" and build a consensus across different Departments while jointly implementing at least 60 measures upon 22 strategic aspects.(2) We have set the strategic direction for the "Cross-Domain Governance and Innovation Ecosystem" to support an innovative environment for a circular economy, revolutionizing the resource utilization model, and create circular value.6. Develop waste management: Policies such as "restrictions on the consumption of disposal plastic products", "furniture recycling and repair", "reuse of kitchen waste", "recycling and reuse of difficult-to-classify waste", and " dual-use bags" were introduced to reduce domestic waste and ensure users pay for the waste. To cut down resource waste, there are measures to reduce the volume of kitchen waste and to encourage the recycling and reuse of kitchen waste. The reuse of bottom ash and fly ash from incineration, trench slurry and earth is promoted. Products made with recycled bottom ash are prioritized for use in public engineering projects within the City to ensure the complete reuse of bottom ash.7. Sustainable food development: The City's three main axes of agricultural activity focused on "recreational edible agriculture, leisure therapy and resilient sustainability," allowing the agricultural land to serve the functions of maintaining diversified ecology, regulating climate, flood-resisting and mitigation, water conservation and purification, recreational tourism, and food and agriculture education, etc. It is also in line with the Ministry of the Interior's land-use plan for the Guandu Plain area, preserving a piece of green land for the next generation, and bringing people, farmers, land, industry and the environment viable and revitalized prospects in urban agriculture.

response_answer: In order to build a livable and sustainable city and to address the climate warming hazards caused by the greenhouse effect, Taipei City conducted a city-level greenhouse gas inventory on its own. The "Taipei City Energy Saving and Carbon Reduction Program" has been promoted in 2008, and in 2016, the "Taipei City Greenhouse Gas Control Implementation Plan" was formulated to strengthen the division of work among various competent authorities to jointly assume responsibility for greenhouse gas reduction in the City. In accordance with international climate agreements and the Greenhouse Gas Reduction and Management Act, the City formulated the "Taipei City Greenhouse Gas Control Implementation Plan" in 2019.The City's Greenhouse Gas Control Implementation Plan (Phase 1) was promoted from 2018 to 2020, and the "Greenhouse Gas Reduction Steering Committee" was established, with the mayor as the convener, to supervise the implementation of energy saving and carbon reduction action plans of four major city government sectors (residential and commercial, transportation, waste, and agriculture and forestry) every quarter, and invite experts and scholars to jointly discuss. In addition, the target of 8% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions in 2020 compared to the base year (2005) was set, and the total emissions in 2020 were 11,388,000 tons, showing a 12.9% reduction compared to the base year, achieving and exceeding the original target of 8% reduction. 1. Target to complete the replacement of 140,440 public streetlights with LED and other energy-saving lamps by the end of 2020: Completed the replacement of 150,930 LED streetlights in the whole City.3. Target to reach 84.51% of the population with access to wastewater treatment by the end of 2020: 85.58% of the population with access to wastewater treatment.4. Target to increase the area of green resources in the City by 250,000m2 by the end of 2020: Increased the area of green resources by about 265,000m2.5. Target to reach 66.8% of the green transportation market share by 2020: Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the percentage of public transportation ridership was affected, and the percentage of people using and taking green transportation reached 60.1%

response_answer: 1. Drought refers to “prolonged period when precipitation is less than normal, which caused deficiency in reservoir, which cannot meet the water demand in the socio-economic system.” 70% of Taiwan’s water comes from typhoons and rainy seasons, with average annual rainfall of 2,000mm, and water storage is difficult due to steep mountains and short river streams. In 2020, the rainy season in Taiwan was short, with no invasion of typhoons, and very little rainfall during the wet season. This led to the most severe drought over the past 56 years, and many counties and cities in Taiwan faced water restrictions. According to the National Science and Technology Center for Disaster Reduction (NCDR), the risk of drought and public water supply in the dry season (from November to April) shows rising trend under the impact of climate change. Based on the scenario of high greenhouse gas emissions (RCP8.5), Taipei’s regional drought hazard level is at 1 or 2 in the base period (1979-2003), and is expected to rise to level 5 by the end of the 21st century. In addition, the standardized precipitation index - three-month accumulation period (SPI3) was used to assess drought intensity, indicating that the peak drought and maximum time lag both occurred in Northern Taiwan. The drought problem will become more serious in the future, which will directly or indirectly affect the citizen’s consumption, economic development and ecological environment.2. Droughts may limit the use of the general water supply system for citizens. Additional water sources must be purchased to maintain production and citizens’ livelihood needs if necessary. This will have a more serious impact on low-income households. In addition, droughts can lead to insufficient water for cleaning, which can affect the environmental sanitation and impact on the health of disadvantaged groups.3. Droughts may prevent the operations of some high water consumption processes in the manufacturing and hospitality industries due to water restrictions, reducing or suspending hospitality services and events and productions.

response_answer: In order to promote the City's net zero transformation, the City proposed the "Taipei City Net Zero Emission Management Autonomy Act" , which was revised after public hearings and consultation with various sectors. Incorporating the 2050 net zero emissions target into this Act, specifying the authorities and responsibilities of various city government agencies, introducing a "carbon budget" system, and setting up a climate transformation fund. In response to the United Nations IPCC AR6 ,the Act will be strengthened with a special chapter on adaptation. The Act is divided into 7 chapters and 55 articles.1. In order to increase the carbon reduction to 40% by 2030, with a net zero emissions target by 2050. Also, promote a "carbon budget", set carbon emission caps for various sectors.2. In order to promote industrial transformation, City will set up a climate transformation fund, which will be dedicated to climate change adaptation, greenhouse gas reduction, and taking care of the underprivileged in climate transformation to ensure fair transformation.3.  It specifies that public buildings and buildings of a certain size in Taipei City should publicly label information on building energy consumption and strengthen controls from 2030 onward to improve building energy efficiency.4.  From the public sector to private sector, the City government has set 2023 as the target year for electrification of public motorcycles and 2030 as the target date for electrification of urban buses and public cars as the key policy priority.  Low-carbon transportation zones will be promoted gradually toreduce the amount of carbon emissions from transportation.5. The Act  stipulates the reduction and banning of the use of disposable items, that the use of tableware should be paid for and completely banned, and requires public and private venues to set up environmentally friendly container recycling systems. In addition, it stipulates that existing old incinerators should be upgraded to high-efficiency green energy power plants and environmentally friendly green energy recycling parks, and carbon capture and utilization equipment should be introduced.6. The Act  stipulates that the City Government should conduct studies and surveys on the City's land use,vulnerability and regularly review urban plans. https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/en/news/4579962

response_answer: Stabilize the quality of water supply and strengthen disaster resiliencehttps://www.water.gov.taipei/News_Video.aspx?n=B6B1A0AF7FC35542&sms=DC950B8D3E3A1744To prevent the turbidity of raw water from exceeding the processing capacity of water treatment facilities during heavy rainfall, the Northern Water Treatment Plant has initiated the Feicui Raw Water Pipeline Project. This project involves the installation of a dedicated intake at the downstream of the Feicui Reservoir, spanning approximately 2.8 kilometers. It allows for the direct extraction of clean water from the Beishi River, with a daily capacity of 2.7 million metric tons, during periods of high turbidity in the Nanshi River. The extracted water is then subject to purification treatment to ensure a stable water supply to the greater Taipei area, thereby achieving sustainable development goals. The tunnel has already been fully connected on May 12, 2023, and the entire project is expected to be completed and operational by 2024.

response_answer: Implementation of the Green Building Autonomy Act https://www.laws.taipei.gov.tw/lawsystem/wfLaw_ArticleContent.aspx?LawID=P13K1008-20200706&RealID=13-11-1008&PN=ALL In order to construct a living environment that is energy saving and carbon reduction, green and water-preserving, and environmentally sustainable, the City passed the "Taipei City Green Building Autonomy Act" in 2014, which stipulates that new buildings of a certain size or larger and publicly-owned new buildings should be regulated to indirectly affect developers, builders, equipment manufacturers, and residents. The construction and management teams are required to obtain the evaluation system for Ecology-Energy Saving-Waste Reduction-Health (EEWH), which includes indicators of biodiversity, greenery, water conservation, daily energy saving, carbon dioxide reduction, waste reduction, indoor environment, water resources, and sewage and waste improvement, etc. Through this, buildings that obtain the Green Building Label can reduce electricity and water consumption by 20% and 30%.The City Government reviews the appropriateness of the regulations on a rolling basis every year, and amended the provisions on photovoltaic power equipment, rainwater storage utilization rate, and domestic waste water recycling rate in 2020 according to the actual implementation. In addition, the City requires new public buildings of a certain size or larger and new non-public buildings to obtain a green building label. In 2021, there were 138 cases which were required to obtain a green building label in accordance with the relevant regulations.

column_name: Describe the risks to your jurisdiction related to the transition to a low-carbon economy
response_answer: Following the net-zero emission pathway and strategy, Taipei City will face the problems of growing electricity demand and energy transition. Electrification is the main trend of net-zero. As the City is highly urbanized, nearly 70% of the carbon emissions come from electricity use. The equipment used in the households and the service industry should be electrified, and as there is new electricity demand for electric vehicles, there is an urgent need to expand the development of decarbonized power such as renewable energy. However, due to the constraints of terrain and a small hinterland, the City continues to promote the “Taipei Chase the Sun Project.” It uses the limited space in the city to promote the development of solar energy using the 4 major directions, which are tenders for municipal properties, subsidies for private installation, promotion of smart grids, and establishment of power plants run jointly by the public and private sectors. It also actively evaluates biomass energy, small hydropower, geothermal energy, and other models, and strengthens energy transformation through central and local cooperation.In addition, the city has included hydrogen into its net-zero pathway, and its emerging energy still faces issues such as establishing a competent authority, integrating necessary regulations including technology, supply and demand, hydrogen transportation facility standards, hydrogen fueling station setting standards, Occupational Safety and Health, and fire protection regulations. The City submitted to the central government to speed up the completion to facilitate the implementation of the application for the locals and industries.The net-zero transition process has resulted in the transformation of gas stations into charging stations (or hydrogen fueling stations) and the unemployment of traditional automotive maintenance personnel. The City has also formulated the “Taipei City Self-Government Ordinance for Net-Zero Emissions” (draft), established a climate transition fund, counseled and subsidized the transformation of SMEs, assisted laborers and disadvantaged groups affected by climate change to change careers, and reduced the cost of transformation to ensure and implement a just transformation.

response_answer: To improve the stability of the water supply in Taipei City, and to cope with risks such as desiccation and water shortage while ensuring the water quality of the water supply, Taipei City Government plans to achieve the goal by increasing the sewage system management rate, proper treatment rate and increasing the proportion of the population supplied with tap water.As the turbidity of Nanshi Stream exceeds 12,000 NTU due to Typhoon Soudelor and Typhoon Dujuan in 2015, the peak and time of turbidity of the Nanshi River raw water were significantly higher than before. Considering the high level of turbidity when heavy rainfalls and typhoons occur in the future, it will still cause a crisis in the water supply in the Taipei area. In addition, the turbidity of raw water in the Feitsui Reservoir is low. If only the raw water of the Beishi River can be taken during the heavy rainfall and avoid the high turbidity of the raw water of the Nanshi River, we can reduce the workload of the water purification plant. Therefore, Taipei Water Department actively promotes the Feitsui original water pipeline, and it has been evaluated by a professional consulting company and assisted by hydraulic experts and scholars to check and confirm the feasible plan. When the water turbidity in the Nanshi River is high, we directly use the relatively clean water source of the Beishi River to reduce the risk of water supply and to ensure the stability and safety of water supply in Taipei Metropolitan Area. It is also to protect industrial activities (including water for people's livelihood) from being affected by water outages during heavy rain and high turbidity. The Taipei Water Department will also benefit from supporting water usage areas in nearby areas.

response_answer: Heatwave warning mechanismhttps://www.dep.gov.taipei/News_Content.aspx?n=9086C3ED2A4F6A09&sms=9B5E42F97878D232&s=89848F0E2E80CC5CThe temperature of the subtropical monsoon climate in Taipei City ranges from 16-30°C. However, it is difficult to dissipate heat in Taipei basin, which may easily cause heat island effect and raise temperature up to 35°C, and further hit record high at 39.7°C in 2020. In order to mitigate the threat of high temperature to the health of citizens, Taiwan’s heat wave warning mechanism was incorporated into the regional disaster prevention and protection plan in 2016, which stipulate that the relevant institutions shall initiate response measures when standards for notification and warning are reached. There were 81 heat wave warnings in 2016-2022, and the measures and achievements of various government departments are as follows:(1) The Department of Environmental Protection uses reclaimed water for sprinkling to cool the surface temperature of roads. The temperature of asphalt pavement can reach above 50°C under high temperature, while the temperature can be reduced by 10°C after sprinkling, and reduce road dust. About 5,443km of roads was sprinkled.(2) To improve the survival rate of plants and green cover ratio, the Parks and Street Lights Office uses recycled water for plant irrigation and prevent plants from drying up under high temperature. The high vegetation cover may improve the microclimate and cool down the city. The total area of plant irrigation was 7,062,134sqm.(3) In order to prevent food poisoning and spoilage under high temperature, the Department of Health has incorporated food preservation in its routine audits and counseling, so that food companies will become more aware of the environment and temperature for preserving food and ingredients, as well as the expiry date and the implementation of hygiene management to mitigate the effect of heat wave on food. 1,715 counseling activities in the food industry, and 6,893 advocacies of food safety to markets and vendors in cooperation with the Taipei City Market Administration Office.(4) In order to prevent heat stress to outdoor workers, the Department of Labor launched the Summer Outdoor Worker Heat Stress On-Site Inspection, and urged enterprises and on-site management personnel to attach great importance in implementing the preventive measures for heat stress, such as installation of effective sun shades, water spraying systems, rest areas, and drinking water supplies. There were a total of 1,778 heat stress worker inspections.(5) The Department of Social Welfare appoints social workers and volunteers to care for the physically and mentally disabled and elderlies that live alone, and provides related heat relief equipment, notifying short-term summer shelters near the residence, in order to mitigate health risks of the disadvantaged people under extreme temperature. Up until now, it has provided care for 90,364 people, including elderlies, the disabled and homeless people.The aforementioned policies and measures are adopted to reduce the threat and negative impact of heat wave in Taipei City.

column_name: Describe the impacts on vulnerable populations and sectors^
response_answer: 1. Heavy rain, defined as precipitation accumulation of 80mm or more in 24 hours or rainfall intensity of 40mm per hour or more, poses challenges in the Taipei Basin due to its mountainous surroundings. This leads to floods, landslides, and debris flows. Research by Taipei City reveals a 4-10% probability of flooding in the 12 districts of Taipei, with higher estimates under high greenhouse gas emission scenarios.2. Short-term heavy rainfall exceeding 80mm per hour triggers widespread flooding and flash floods in mountainous areas, endangering lives and destroying habitats. It also contaminates water sources, increasing the presence of microorganisms like Escherichia coli in estuaries. This poses health risks to drinking water, vegetables, and fruits, especially for vulnerable groups like the elderly and children under 5 years old. Prolonged waterlogging damage farmlands, leading to crop losses in agriculture, fishing, and animal husbandry industries. It also disrupts transportation, damages urban roads, power supply systems, and hampers waste disposal and water supply operations.3. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change's 6th Assessment Report projects precipitation changes in Taiwan in the mid to late 21st century. Under a worst-case scenario, annual total rainfall is expected to increase by 15-31%, and the average annual maximum one-day rainfall intensity is projected to increase by 20-41.3%. The number of typhoons affecting Taiwan is predicted to decrease by 15-55%, but the proportion of intense typhoons may rise by 100-500%.4. Taipei has two flood-prone locations with historical water accumulation exceeding 50 centimeters: Zhumei area in Beitou District and Guandu Plain. Preservation of the natural ecology in Guandu has hindered the implementation of a comprehensive flood control and drainage system. Similarly, undecided urban planning in the Shezidao area of Shilin District prevents the establishment of a comprehensive flood control and drainage system.

Although the development of renewable energy is limited by geographical conditions, the City, with its goal of 2050 net zero emissions, will also strive to meet the national policy 2025 renewable energy accounting for 20% of the target, actively develop diversified energy, and work with the country to achieve a 2050 renewable energy rate of 60-70%, hydrogen energy of 9-12%, and other renewable energy targets. In addition, the City will continue to promote biogas recovery for power generation, improve the efficiency of incinerator, power generation equipment, and promote the renewal of the operating components of the Feitsui Reservoir Power Plant to enhance power generation efficiency. response_answer: Taiwan is located in a high-risk area, and under the influence of global climate change, various major disasters have occurred frequently, causing loss of life and property and threatening the safety of the community and the city.In view of the recent climate change and extreme weather effects, not only has the scale of disasters increased, but also the frequency of disasters. In order to reduce the impact of natural disasters on the City, it has become an important issue to promote a resilient city by the method adopted by the international community. Therefore, in 2021, the Taipei City Fire Department, through a professional service project, made reference to the indicators and scorecard proposed by the United Nations for the establishment of a resilient city, and established localized resilient city assessment indicators suitable for use in the City by adopting the suggestions of experts and scholars in various fields and joint discussions with the relevant government agencies to achieve the purpose of building a resilient city. In addition, the results of the project were published and disseminated in international exchange occasions to raise the international profile of the City's disaster prevention and mitigation efforts.

response_answer: Dengue Fever Preventionhttps://data.taipei/dataset/detail?id=aa397ee2-9e39-44b9-9d0d-d88a16987a3f1. Through the "Capital Metropolitan Area Dengue Fever Prevention and Control Plan," the city integrates relevant departments, including health, environmental protection, civil affairs, and education, to collaborate across bureaus and implement preventive measures during both regular periods and local dengue fever outbreaks. The goal is to prevent the occurrence of community clusters of dengue fever infections.2. As of 2022, the city has collaborated with 99 medical institutions to establish the "Building Dengue Fever Epidemic Prevention Network and Community Clinic Rapid Screening Reporting" system. This facilitates early detection of confirmed dengue fever cases and enables prompt medical treatment, thereby preventing the escalation of the epidemic.3. Utilizing the Geographic Information System (GIS) for infectious disease control, the city collects data on the density of disease-carrying mosquitoes in high-risk community areas such as vacant houses, vacant lots, and markets. This information provides epidemic prevention personnel with precise epidemiological and geographical data to facilitate targeted prevention and control measures.4. The city recruits and trains 12 district-level epidemic prevention teams to strengthen local community and school mosquito control and promote awareness of dengue fever prevention. This effort enhances their epidemic prevention knowledge and enables them to quickly mobilize and control outbreaks during emergencies, thereby strengthening the community's epidemic prevention capacity.

response_answer: To improve the stability of the water supply in Taipei City, and to cope with risks such as desiccation and water shortage while ensuring the water quality of the water supply, Taipei City Government plans to achieve the goal by increasing the sewage system management rate, proper treatment rate and increasing the proportion of the population supplied with tap water.As the turbidity of Nanshi Stream exceeds 12,000 NTU due to Typhoon Soudelor and Typhoon Dujuan in 2015, the peak and time of turbidity of the Nanshi River raw water were significantly higher than before. Considering the high level of turbidity when heavy rainfalls and typhoons occur in the future, it will still cause a crisis in the water supply in the Taipei area. In addition, the turbidity of raw water in the Feitsui Reservoir is low. If only the raw water of the Beishi River can be taken during the heavy rainfall and avoid the high turbidity of the raw water of the Nanshi River, we can reduce the workload of the water purification plant. Therefore, Taipei Water Department actively promotes the Feitsui original water pipeline, and it has been evaluated by a professional consulting company and assisted by hydraulic experts and scholars to check and confirm the feasible plan. When the water turbidity in the Nanshi River is high, we directly use the relatively clean water source of the Beishi River to reduce the risk of water supply and to ensure the stability and safety of water supply in Taipei Metropolitan Area. It is also to protect industrial activities (including water for people's livelihood) from being affected by water outages during heavy rain and high turbidity. The Taipei Water Department will also benefit from supporting water usage areas in nearby areas.

response_answer: 1.Taiwan is in the East Asian monsoon region and along the main path of typhoons in the northwest Pacific. Statistics show that Taiwan is affected by approximately 3.9 typhoons each year, which often bring strong winds and heavy rainfall, leading to natural disasters. Due to its basin terrain, Taipei is prone to flooding, inundation, and even debris flows during typhoon events. According to the National Science and Technology Center for Disaster Reduction (NCDR) and international research estimates, there is a decreasing trend in the number of typhoons affecting Taiwan in the future. However, the frequency of intense typhoon formation and the average rainfall intensity of typhoons are both increasing. The proportion of intense typhoons is projected to rise from 2.12% during the base period (1986-2005) to 5.59% by the end of the 21st century. This will result in more severe weather and wind-related disasters, impacting the city's infrastructure and the safety of its residents.2. Typhoon-related disasters can mainly be divided into strong winds and heavy rainfall. Strong winds can cause road signs, utility poles, and trees to collapse, and may also damage telecommunication and power lines, leading to widespread power outages and chaotic road traffic, posing hazards to pedestrians and vehicles. Heavy rainfall can cause multiple landslides and debris flows in mountainous areas, leading to tree collapse, destruction of natural habitats, and even human casualties. When necessary, evacuation notices must be issued to ensure the safety of residents and old settlements in flood- and debris flow-prone areas. Vulnerable groups such as the elderly, women, and children may face greater challenges during evacuations. Additionally, low-income households will require increased support for post-disaster reconstruction and remedial measures.3. Heavy rainfall caused by typhoons can result in river overflowing and urban flooding, severely impacting transportation systems such as the metro and highways. Severe urban flooding can also lead to disruptions and losses in the food and beverage service industry, and outdoor workers such as construction workers will be unable to carry out their duties. Typhoon-related precipitation and strong winds can damage the power supply system and hinder the operation of waste disposal and water supply systems.

question_name: Provide details on your climate risk and vulnerability assessment.
response_answer: Human activities consume a lot of fossil fuels and forest resources, and disrupt the Earth's natural environment system and greenhouse gas circulation mechanism, leading to global warming and climate changes, and causing extreme climate events significantly increased. United Nations Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Changes Committee (IPCC) reports also pointed out that, since the 1950s, the Earth's warming and human activities are highly related (more than 90%). However, the implementation of mitigation strategies, which is reducing greenhouse gas emissions, will not be able to immediately improve the climate change impacts (carbon dioxide in the atmosphere remnants subsequent impact will continue for 50 to 200 years). Therefore, in addition to continued commitment to energy-saving and greenhouse gas emissions mitigation strategy, how to change through social and economic development patterns, prompting humans to adapt to the impacts of climate change, reduce the level of impacts of climate change, and in order to survive in the extreme climate effects, it is equally important to mitigate strategies.This project is sponsored by the Council for Economic Planning and Development, and using Taipei city as the demonstration area. The concept of strategic planning, rolling wave planning, and bottom-up approach are used in the whole planning process. Many seminars, meetings of the working platform fully with the Taipei City Government are conducted to communicate and coordinate with different sectors in the city government to get the consensus. The main project content are: (1) to establish the climate change adaptation planning framework and platform; (2) to analyzes the trends and the impact of climate change; (3) to clarify the impact of climate change in key sector with the concept of Vulnerability; (4) analysis the impact of climate change vulnerability;(5) analysis of the key issues; (6) review both policy and related programs;(7) proposal of climate change adaptation strategy and action plan.More than 40 times of meetings, seminars, and interviews were held in ten months, through the system analysis approach, this project made a total of 185 action plans. Four action plans have co-benefit with six other sectors. 162 action plans have co-benefit with at least one other sector. Only 8 action plans have trade-off with other sector. This project is a preliminary project for the first year, and should be continued in the future rolling reviewed and included in the annual implementation policy.

response_answer: From 2003 to 2004, Taipei City Government began to develop the "Integrated Water Management Plan".The main goal of the integrated water management plan is to reduce flooding and improve the overall capacity of the drainage system by taking measures through the proposed actionable items of integrated water management, such as sewer storage sharing, flood control pond sharing, watershed outflow suppression facility sharing, and drainage system improvement to ensure that drainage facilities meet the 5-year recurrence period storm drainage protection standard. Water retentionis then promoted through river basin sharing to provide a margin when the rainfall exceeds the drainage standards.In 2015, Taipei City Government further promoted the sponge city policy to bring the urban water environment to a new level, based on its long-standing promotion of "integrated water management" for urban flood-resisting and safety. The sponge city policy outlines the future vision of Taipei City with "resilient water adaptation", "sustainable water use", and "friendly water environment”. The policy is based on six major goals, namely, "sound urban water circulation", "improved flood-resisting capacity", "diversified and active water use", "stable and efficient water supply", "ecologically diverse water habitats", and "enriched and attractive water recreation” as the direction for the campaign. Finally, the policy adopts twelve promotion strategies, including "water permeability and greening of public facilities", "water permeability and greening of private sector buildings", "urban river basin measures", "public-private partnership for intelligent disaster prevention", "wastewater recycling", "rainwater and groundwater utilization", "sound water supply system for catchment management", "water efficiency improvement", "environmental restoration of wetlands", "water quality improvement of rivers and streams", "water-friendly construction of rivers and streams" and "promotion of water activities along the riverbanks" , which are taken as the implementation goals. Through engineering, management, and legal measures, and incorporating the concepts of open government, public participation, and public-private collaboration, the City Government will develop relevant promotion strategies and implementation plans, which will be implemented and promoted by various agencies of the City Government to jointly build Taipei into a safe, sustainable, and ecological sponge city.

response_answer: Re-use of incineration bottom residueshttps://www.dep.gov.taipei/News_Content.aspx?n=CB6D5C560DE4D2DD&s=35E226B482A85178Since 2003, in collaboration with the Northern Taiwan Joint Recycling Program and by outsourcing to professional companies, efforts have been made to reuse bottom ash instead of landfill disposal. Starting in September 2005, all bottom ash has been fully outsourced for recycling. After the screening, magnetic separation, and manual sorting of metal waste, the stabilized materials are further processed into incineration recycled aggregates. These aggregates are then utilized in asphalt concrete, road construction, pipe backfilling projects, and graded aggregates. Since June 1, 2021, applications for road excavation projects in Taipei City have been required to include plans for using incineration recycled aggregates. This not only helps achieve the goal of completely recycling bottom ash, but also promotes resource circulation, local utilization, and environmental sustainability. Over the past five years (2018-2022), Taipei City has recycled approximately 489,000 metric tons of bottom ash, with an average of 97,800 tons per year.The carbon reduction calculation estimates that replacing natural sand and gravel with each metric ton of recycled aggregates can reduce approximately 13.7 kg of CO2-e emissions.The fly ash from Muzha Plant and Beitou Plant is washed and sent to cement plants as raw materials for cement production. Additionally, some of the washed fly ash from Beitou Plant is reused in non-structural brick products and applied in the high-temperature smelting process of steel making dust, effectively utilizing waste as valuable industrial resources. Over the past five years (2018-2022), Taipei City has recycled approximately 24,000 metric tons of fly ash, with an average of 4,803 tons per year.The carbon reduction calculation estimates that replacing each metric ton of washed fly ash with cement raw materials can reduce approximately 940 kg of CO2-e emissions.

The flood-resisting plan of Taipei area is to apply the methods of "flood storage", "flood discharge", "flood diversion", and "flood control". In addition to the construction of embankments along the Tamsui River and its tributaries, because of the dense housing around the Taipei Bridge, which made it impossible to widen the river pass and the formation of the urban areas on both sides of the Keelung River, the Erchong Floodway and the Yuanshanzih Sluiceway were built to divert the flood waters of the Xindian River, the Dahan River, and the Keelung River. After the completion of the project, the whole Tamsui River basin flood-resisting system can prevent major floods for a 200-year recurrence period.

Precautions for i-Voting online voting operations have been formulated and continuously promoted. The operational procedures for implementing citizen participation in public works and urban planning projects have been improved, taking into account public opinions and administrative efficiency. Taipei City has established a Citizen Participation Network and actively updates citizen participation activities and progress of government agencies in real-time, utilizing the official Line account for precise delivery and push notifications. The city also focuses on information disclosure and promotes the use of the Taipei City Open Data Platform for legitimate purposes, providing access to a wide range of information. Additionally, participatory budgeting efforts are ongoing, with regular proposal seminars, residents' meetings, workshops, and voting in district offices. Collaboration with academia helps analyze past information and improve participatory budgeting practices.

response_answer: The compilation of the City's Voluntary Local Report stemmed from the conclusion reached in the 44th meeting of the City's Council for Sustainable Development in July 2016. It was decided that the reports should compare existing sustainable development indicators from the City's strategic roadmap with the ISO 37120 indicators of the World Council on City Data (WCCD) and the UN SDG indicators. In-depth evaluations and analyses of various indicators based on the SDG indicators will also be conducted in order to adjust the composition and structure of the Council's work accordingly. After numerous rounds of collaborations between government agencies and negotiations with experts and scholars, the Council decided on the priority promotion SDGs at the 49th Council meeting in November 2017. Based on Taipei City's existing sustainable development goals and strategic roadmap, the Council established tasks corresponding to various SDGs, proposing or amending strategies, visions, goals, and action plans accordingly.In March 2019, Mayor Ko, Wen-Je visited the US. While in New York, he spoke about the progress Taipei City had made to promote sustainable development in line with the SDGs. During the meeting, he also announced plans to follow New York's footsteps, prioritize SDG 3, 6, 7, 11, 12, 13, and 17 with the mindset of “Global Perspective, Taipei Action”, and officially published the “Sustainable Development Goals - Taipei City Voluntary Local Review” in September 2019.In 2020, the City continued the outcome of the 2019 Voluntary Local Review, reexamining the 17 SDGs and their connection to the City. Considering the importance of education, gender equality, economic development, and infrastructure, the City decided to prioritize four additional SDGs - SDG 4, 5, 8, and 9. Additionally, many of the epidemic prevention measures taken in response to the COVID-19 pandemic also echoed the seven prioritiy SDGs. In September 2020, the City officially published the 2nd version of “Sustainable Development Goals - Taipei City Voluntary Local Review”, continuing to make rolling reviews and adjustments to various tasks and regularly disclosing the results, gradually moving toward the goal of becoming a “Livable and Sustainable city”.Climate actions are closely related to sustainable development. On Earth Day, April 22, 2021, Taipei City mayor Ko Wen-Je announced that “Taipei City will courageously shoulder its international responsibility to reduce global carbon emissions, pursue the goal of net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, and work with the rest of the world to ensure climate safety”. Therefore, the VLR report this year (2022) will focus on SDG 13 - Climate Action, showcasing the connections and relevant results of various SDGs and climate actions to gradually move towards achieving sustainable development and the goal of net-zero emissions by 2050.

question_name: Report your jurisdiction's most significant examples of collaboration with government, business, and/or civil society on climate-related issues.
response_answer: In July 2018, the Taipei City Government promulgated the “Taipei City Kitchen Waste Reduction Action Plan” to promote its citizens to “buy, cook, and order it after thinking about it.” In 2021, the discharge of kitchen waste is reduced by 20% compared with 2018.1. The Department of Environmental Protection’s kitchen waste reduction started with the 157 Happy Miles activities, encouraging citizens to exchange recyclables for kitchen waste drain strainer to drain kitchen waste to achieve the reduction goal. The City Government, 12 administrative district offices, MRT video wall, youtube, Mayor Ko's Facebook, yahoo homepage has broadcasted the promotional video on “Cherish Food, Empty Plates, Zero Waste,” with a total of 7 million views. Through the transmission of the concept of cherish food in the video, it transforms awareness of cherish food in the eco-friendly environment into practical actions, embed it in the lives of all citizens, and implement cherishing of food, empty plates, and zero waste. The Department of Environmental Protection has organized 84 advocacy activities with communities, schools and enterprises to convey the concept of food saving, “eat, buy, cook the amount of food you can finish”concept. In addition, composts from kitchen waste (mainly fruit peel and seeds, tea leaves, coffee grounds, and bones) cannot be reduced through food cherishing as it is inedible. Since 2020, the three incineration plants have set up kitchen waste pre-treatment facilities, which will reduce household kitchen waste by crushing, dehydrating, and reducing its volume and area by about 64%, effectively improving the quality of compost and shortening the processing time for reuse.2. The Department of Education actively requires manufacturers to provide the agency's monthly kitchen waste amount and evaluate the reasons for the leftover food according to the school lunch bidding and implementation specifications. They also set an upper limit on the number of prepared meals (such as 3% of the ordered meals) as a reference for a reasonable amount of backup. In addition, they cooperated with industries of the same trade to review the leftovers on weekdays and adjust the cooking methods and menus. According to the statistics of the CBM, the kitchen waste from daily lunches in 2016 was about 10 tons. With the city's active promotion and the full cooperation of schools at all grade levels, the average kitchen waste from daily lunches in 2021 has been reduced to 2~3 tons.3. The Secretariat in the City Hall Building of the Taipei City Government has supported the implementation of the kitchen waste reduction policy since 2018. Kitchen waste is reduced from the source by accurately calculating the number of diners in the canteen and preparing the ingredients. Kitchen waste reduction is promoted in the city hall building. For the sharing of leftovers, the canteen provides imperfect ingredients, bean dregs, and coffee dregs for reuse every day. For the end of the reduction, from 2019, the kitchen waste treatment equipment is leased and handled using the preliminary gravity drainage method, which is the most efficient and cost-effective method. The amount of kitchen waste in 2021 is 0.17 (metric ton/day), which is reduced by 32% compared to the base year (2018).4. The Department of Environmental Protection has been promoting the “Taipei City Food Saving Pact” since 2019, inviting food service-related industries to sign it together. The contents include encouraging customers to order the amount of food they will be able to finish, properly managing the purchase of appropriate amount of ingredients, and implementing kitchen waste recycling. The DEP also works with industries to reduce food waste from the source and recycle at the back-end to reduce food waste together. The cumulative amount of food waste is reduced by 4,312.11 metric tons by 2021. The result of the agreement to reduce food waste: In 2021, a total of 56 enterprises, 432 food services, institutional food services, department stores, hotels, hypermarkets, fast food restaurants, and other relevant industries signed an agreement to reduce food waste.5. Taipei City Government established a food exchange platform since 2016. The platform works with 7 public markets and the Taipei Agricultural Products Marketing Corporation. This platform encourages vendors to donate their fresh edible vegetables and fruits to social welfare organizations after the market closes so they can prepare and provide them to the service recipients or distribute them to disadvantaged households. Relevant results are shown below:(1) 7 public markets and the Taipei Agricultural Products Marketing Corporation have joined the food exchange platform as of the end of 2021. (2) According to statistics, from 2016 to 2021, a total of 59,789kg were donated, with 116,440 beneficiaries, realizing the shared value of sustainable food.
