response_answer: Taipei City has conducted an independent greenhouse gas inventory operation at the city level, showing a gradual decrease in emissions from 13.074 million metric tons of CO2e in 2005, in 2021, greenhouse gas emissions were 11.1426 million metric tons of CO2e, representing a reduction of approximately 1.9311 million metric tons compared to 2005, a decrease of 14.77%.The main sources of greenhouse gas emissions in the city are the residential, commercial, and transportation sectors, accounting for approximately 95% of the total emissions. To achieve energy-saving and carbon reduction goals, the city initially focused on the public sector and formulated an energy-saving plan for the Taipei City Government and affiliated agencies. The city government implemented measures to promote energy-saving and carbon reduction in the industrial and commercial sectors. These measures include energy-saving counseling, law enforcement and advocacy, incentive subsidies, and the promotion of energy-saving products. On-site inspections of energy-consuming equipment are conducted, and compliance with regulations is ensured. The promotion of energy-saving products is carried out through cooperation with various stores. In 2021, the service sector's electricity consumption decreased by 349 million kWh compared to 2020, resulting in an electricity saving rate of 3.77%.Solar photovoltaic systems have been installed on government agencies and schools, resulting in significant power generation and carbon reduction. Citizen power plants managed by civic groups have been established on city-owned buildings. Landfill sites are being transformed into energy parks, and small hydropower generation systems are being introduced. The city is also actively promoting the electrification of vehicles. An electric vehicle subsidy program has been announced, and charging stations are being constructed. response_answer: 1. According to the definition of the Soil and Water Conservation Bureau of the Council of Agriculture, debris flows refer to a natural phenomenon that constitutes a mixture of substances, such as mud, sand, gravel, boulder, and water. It is a fluid object produced due to gravity, and it flows from high places to low places and along the slope surface or ditches. If debris flows result in casualties, damaged buildings, bridges or public infrastructures, and loss of life or property, it can be called “debris flow hazard.” Taiwan has established a rainfall threshold value for debris flow warning. It is based on the rainfall data from the Central Weather Bureau; the rainfall triggering index (RTI) is produced by multiplying Effective Accumulated Rainfall (Rt) by Rainfall Intensity (I). The rainfall warning value of the debris flow is calculated by statistical methods. It is then simplified into accumulated rainfall values, which can be used as a reference rainfall warning value for various regions to evaluate the time of debris flow prevention and evacuation.2. There are 50 potential debris flow torrents in Taipei City. When the debris flow occurs, the soil and riverbed in the drainage area are scraped deeply, and the vegetation and debris on the sideslope are also washed away. The foot of the mountain or the exit of the valley is often an area where debris flows accumulate, which often leads to the burial of the residential houses and the casualties of the residents. Among them, children and the elderly may face greater difficulty in evacuation due to their difficulty in moving. Outdoor workers are also more likely to be exposed to the risk of debris flow due to their workplace.3. The straightness of the flow direction of the debris flow is clearly seen, and it does not easily change its direction when encountering obstacles or curved roads. Its violent attack will have a direct impact on the forestry and ecological conservation industries. The wires and cables located in its flowing path may also cause damage to the power supply system of the electric power industries. The accumulation phenomenon of debris flow will lead to the diversion of rivers, and block roads and railway tracks, resulting in major traffic accidents, so it also has a considerable impact on the public transportation industry.

response_answer: Net Zero Demonstration for Public Buildingshttps://www.dep.gov.taipei/News_Content.aspx?n=3C6047752EDB7496&s=82B02A650A30277BIn order to strengthen the effectiveness of Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) reviews and enhance environmental benefits, on October 24, 2016, the City issued and implemented the "Taipei City Environmental Impact Assessment Criteria for Promoting a Livable and Sustainable City", which requires that EIA development projects in the City should obtain a silver level or higher green building label and install photovoltaic power generation equipment. In order to move toward 2050 net zero emissions and increase the environmental quality requirements of the City's EIA development project, the City amended the criteria on April 26, 2022, requiring that the Green Building Label be upgraded to gold level and that building energy efficiency be evaluated, that a certain percentage of renewable energy generation equipment or energy storage equipment be installed, that the increase in greenhouse gases during operation be offset, and that measures such as the introduction of smart construction sites be included in the Environmental Impact Statement. After the EIA review and approval, the criteria will be implemented thoroughly. question_name: Report details on the climate action plan or strategy that addresses mitigation, adaptation (resilience), and/or energy-related issues in your jurisdiction.
response_answer: Taipei City has been actively implementing reduction measures, resulting in a decrease in emissions of11.388 million metric tons of CO2e in 2020, representing a 12.9% reduction compared to the baseline year of 2005. The residential, commercial, and transportation sectors are the main sources of emissions, accounting for 74.6% and 20.6% of the city's total emissions, respectively. Emissions from the residential and commercial sectors decreased by 13.1% in 2020 compared to the baseline year, while emissions from the transportation sector decreased by 8.2%.The residential, commercial, and transportation sectors constitute the city's major carbon sources, accounting for 74.60%, 20.58%, and 2.69% of the total emissions, respectively. Together, these three sectors contribute to nearly 98% of the city's carbon emissions.Based on projections of future population and economic changes, it is estimated that without any relevant reduction measures, emissions in 2050 would reach 12.496 million metric tons of CO2e.The promotion of net-zero emissions in Taipei City is pursued through the implementation of smart zero-carbon buildings, green and low-carbon transportation, a circular economy with zero waste, and the enhancement of carbon sinks. A collaboration between the central government and public-private sectors is crucial to achieve the net-zero emissions goal. The main strategies for the three major sectors include energy efficiency inspections, disclosure, and regulations in the residential and commercial sectors, along with the integration of renewable energy and hydrogen use to achieve zero-carbon buildings. The transportation sector focuses on promoting green transportation and the adoption of electric (hydrogen) vehicles. The waste sector aims for a circular economy with zero waste and ultimately zero emissions from waste treatment facilities. The agriculture and forestry sector emphasizes afforestation to increase carbon sinks and strengthens wetland conservation to maintain carbon sequestration.By implementing these strategies, Taipei City aims to achieve its net-zero emissions goal and actively contribute to mitigating climate change.

response_answer: Taipei City Disaster Prevention Info Websitehttps://eoc.gov.taipei/The Taipei City Disaster Prevention Info Website provides information on disaster prevention, weather, water, earthquake, evacuation and shelter, drills and training, disaster checklists, and post-disaster recovery systems. The website provides education and advocacies on disaster prevention for citizens, village chiefs, and disaster prevention personnel, with a total of 185,779 views from 2022 to July 2023. In order to expand the exposure and reach of the message, the website also introduced the dynamic design analysis method, with automatic ranking based on the number of views, forwarding to relevant social networking sites (such as Facebook and Twitter) to enhance the disaster prevention and resilience in Taipei City.In addition, in face of major disasters or risks of occurrence in Taipei City. The competent authorities of disaster prevention and protection have set up disaster prevention centers based on the type, scale, status, and needs of disaster prevention, and the website became the "Disaster Prevention and Protection Information Section", which provides immediate information on hazards such as flooding, earthquakes, and landslides, as well as evacuation and shelter, disaster prevention plans, and casualty lists. The website provides early disaster response measures to citizens and government units, such as flood prevention, landslide, and disaster relief, so as to improve the disaster prevention procedures.

response_answer: In January 2020, the Executive Yuan approved the "Management Plan of Energy Efficiency in Government Agencies and Schools" (2020-2023), taking 2015 as the base year. response_answer: Promoting food waste reductionhttps://www.gov.taipei/plan/News_Content_MCP.aspx?n=61835E60879A5D13&sms=C04230CB75259A56&s=1A02C14B4B10824CPromoting food waste reduction, in order to achieve the goal of food-cherishing and food waste reduction, the Department of Environmental Protection has the “Taipei City Food Waste Reduction Action Plan” promoted to relevant bureaus, sectors, departments, and divisions of Taipei City Government. Promote the concept of “food-cherishing” in accordance with the principle of “from the inside to the outside, from public sector to private sector”. Guide the general public to build up an attitude of “think twice before buying, think twice before cooking, and think twice before ordering” in order to apply the concept of reducing and avoiding food waste into their daily life. In addition to government agencies, enterprises are also actively encouraged to sign the “Food-Cherishing Pact” in order to contribute to having a better use of food resources. The idea is to have the concept of food-cherishing embedded in the heart of Taipei citizens through the leadership of the government and the support of the private sector so to enhance the food waste reduction action of Taipei citizens jointly and achieve the goal of reducing food waste by 3% annually in Taipei City.The household food waste reduction activities of the Department of Environmental Protection started with 157 Happy Village activities, encouraging people to exchange recyclables for food waste drainage sieves and to drain food waste to achieve the reduction target through the "Cherishing Food, Clean Dish, and Zero Waste" promotion video (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6jQH55_RxTk). The video was broadcast on the video wall of City Hall, 12 administrative districts, MRT, YouTube, Mayor Ko's Facebook page, and yahoo home page, etc, and was viewed by 7 million people. By transmitting the concept of food conservation in the video, the environmental protection consciousness of cherishing food is transformed into practical actions and deepened into the life of all citizens to implement cherishing food, clean dish, and zero waste. The Department of Environmental Protection of the City has organized 84 promotional activities in conjunction with communities, schools, and enterprises to convey the concept of "buy and cook as much as you eat” for food conservation. In addition, the composted food waste (mainly fruit peels and seeds, tea leaves, coffee grounds, bones, etc) cannot be reduced through food waste reduction because it is inedible. 1. Due to the high moisture content of household food waste, since 2020, Taipei City has installed pre-treatment equipment for crushing and dehydrating food waste at three municipal incineration plants. The dehydrated composted food waste is then used to produce solid residue for composting, reducing the burden of back-end treatment and improving the willingness to process compost at composting sites.2. In 2022, the municipal cleaning team collected a total of 52,864 metric tons of compostable food waste and vegetable residues. Through crushing and dehydrating, the waste was reduced by 65% and produced 18,502 metric tons of solid residue. It is estimated that this initiative will result in a reduction of approximately 6,494 metric tons of CO2e emissions.

response_answer: In order to realize Taipei City's vision of a "livable and sustainable" city, the Department of Economic Development of Taipei City Government has been working on a new vision and development strategy for Taipei City's future industries since 2019. In the post-pandemic era, the industry needs to learn to live with more uncertainties, and how to make the best use of emerging technologies to build a competitive advantage and create a more resilient development model is an important issue for business operations and even city governance. At this time of rapid changes in the external environment, the "Taipei City 2030 Future Industrial Development Policy White Paper " (this White Paper) is presented as a demonstration of the government's proactive approach to the future industrial development of Taipei City.This White Paper is the collective wisdom of experts from various fields of industry, government, academia, and research, and we propose three key directions for the future industrial development of Taipei City – smart living, healthy living, and a sustainable environment. Under the three key directions, seven key development industries are proposed: A smart retail industry, a convention and exhibition industry, the tourism industry, a digital content industry, a smart health industry, a smart energy industry, and a circular design industry. Industrial development is an important key to building a happy life for citizens, and it is expected to create a positive cycle between industrial development and a "livable and sustainable" city, i.e., promoting the development of emerging industries, helping industries create added value, creating quality jobs, and generating government tax revenue, so that the government can continuously optimize the environment for industrial development.In the future, the Government will use the industrial projects planned in this White Paper to promote the future development of industries in Taipei City with the policy guidelines of "from the inside to the outside" and "from public sector to private sector", and make good use of the existing policy resources to pragmatically promote the development of industries in Taipei City, so as to make Taipei City a model city for the flourishing development of industries and a gateway to national trade and commerce.

question_name: Provide details on your climate risk and vulnerability assessment.
response_answer: The assessment methodology adopted by the City is the “Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD)” and it is an officially recognized framework by which climate risk assessment and management can be executed. The assessment methodology, Taiwan's Climate Change Adaptation Six Steps (CCA6Steps), is mainly based on the IPCC AR5 definition of climate risk in the TaiCCAT project conducted by the Ministry of Science and Technology. The CCA3Steps integrates and combines the steps listed in both domestic and international climate change adaptation frameworks, including the UNDP APF, UKCIP Adaptation Wizard, CLIMATE-ADAPT Adaptation Support Tool, and Taiwan's climate change adaptation plans. In addition, with reference to Taiwan’s climate change adaptation plan, a six-step method for formulating climate change adaptation capacity building is referred to as the “Climate Adaptation Six Steps (CCA-6Steps),” it includes:(1) Identifying Problems and Objectives,(2) Assessing and Analyzing Current Climate Risks,(3) Assessing and Analyzing Future Climate Risks,(4) Identifying Climate Adaptation Options,(5) Planning Climate Adaptation Pathways, and (6) Monitoring and Modifying Climate Adaptation Pathways.The “Climate Risk Template” (aligning with step 2~3 CCA6Steps) and “Climate Risk Maps” (aligning with step 2~4 of CCA6Steps) are proposed as interdisciplinary climate risk analysis tools based on the procedure of CCA6Steps, and the tools are used for Taipei City's climate risk assessment. The Climate Risk Template not only conforms to the vulnerability definition of ISO 14091 and IPCC AR5 and the assessment framework of ISO14092 and IPCC AR5, but also allows the interdisciplinary integration, enabling experts from different research areas to conduct climate risk assessment and risk communication based on the same standards.The City's overall climate change adaptation capacity building is strengthened through interdisciplinary communication and negotiation. In addition, the key contents and results of the discussion on the implementation status of experts and various bureaus are gathered with the concept of dynamic adaptation pathways. The Taipei City climate change adaptation, implementation plan will ultimately be proposed. The preliminary planning of the content of the implementation plan will refer to the content framework of the City's adaptation action plan in 2021. At the same time, we will incorporate the City's past research and analysis results, as well as the City's relevant policy developments and urban visions in recent years, to complete the content of the City's adaptation implementation plan. Disasters, water resources, critical infrastructures, industries and energies, agriculture and biodiversity, land use, and health are the focus of the discussion.The chapters of the City’s climate change adaptation, implementation plan include: (1) Current condition analysis, (2) Project targets, (3) Implementation timetables, (4) Implementation plans, (5) Expected benefits, and (6) Evaluation mechanisms.

response_answer: In response to global climate governance, the City will follow international conventions to move toward the 2050 net zero greenhouse gas emissions target, to fulfill the obligations of global village citizens, and to share the international responsibility for carbon reduction, and on the basis of the 2030 United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (based on the principle of "from the inside to the outside, from public sector to private sector"), to propose a net zero strategic pathway blueprint, to complement the national energy and industrial transformation, and to continuously promote multiple climate actions, regularly review the carbon reduction targets, and gradually realize being a zero-carbon city.This plan seeks to establish a “livable and sustainable city” with “disaster resilience” by advocating and enhancing disaster risk governance and climate change adaptation. In addition to the characteristics of disasters experienced by Taipei City in past years, this plan also keeps up with the international trends for disaster mitigation. On the basis of 2015-2030 Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (SFDRR) developed by “the third UN World Conference on Disaster Risk Reduction” in 2015, all the policies and results in Taipei City were reviewed. Anchored in the perspectives of a local government but aiming for global goals, two plan objectives and four strategic guidelines were mapped out to advocate disaster prevention awareness and capability across-the-board.

response_answer: In order to ensure a smooth and fair implementation of the stipulated climate actions, Taipei City has incorporated the concept of civic participation. In 2015, the “Taipei City Government Citizen Participation Committee" was established, and the "Taipei City Citizen Participation Website" (https://civil.gov.taipei/) was created. The relevant promotions are explained as follows:1. The committee has recruited citizens from outside the government through open selections. This is the 6th term so far. The meeting is held every quarter and the meeting is live-streamed. After the meeting, the meeting minutes are also made public by posting them online.2. Formulate the precautions for i-Voting online voting operations, and continue to promote and publicize.3. Improve the "Operation Procedures for Implementing Citizen Participation System by the Taipei City Government Public Works,” consolidate the “Operation Procedures for Implementing Citizen Participation in the Pilot Implementation of Local Small Public Works of Taipei City Government", and revise the standard operation flow chart and agencies’ self-inspection table at different stages. These are to take into account the public opinions and administrative efficiency, and assist the various agencies of the government to implement citizen participation so that the citizens can effectively convey their opinions to the relevant agencies of the Taipei City Government.4. According to the "Operational Procedures for the Citizen Participation Mechanism of the Taipei City Government Handling the Urban Planning Project Development and Planning," the "Taipei Urban Planning Citizen Participation Section" is planned to be created (https://www.udd.gov.taipei/ProjectPage/ Public Participation) to help the citizens find relevant information easily, increase their understanding of urban planning and develop the ability to participate in urban planning.5. Establish the "Taipei Citizen Participation Network" and continue to innovate and update the citizen participation activities and progress of various government agencies in real time, and combine with the official Line account of the government for precise delivery and push notification subscriptions to facilitate citizens to understand. The City obtained a NCC Accessible conformance level AA on January 7, 2022. From its launch in 2016 to March 31, 2022, 5,113 pieces of citizen participation meeting information have been recorded, with a cumulative number of views of 700,000. In addition, the “Public Works Citizen Participation Section” provides relevant information on major public works of the government and can be linked to the “Public Policy Network Participation Platform" of the National Development Council's “public speaking” discussion section to strengthen the function of online communication and collect public opinion6. Implement information disclosure, and promote information disclosure on the Taipei City Open Data Platform (https://data.taipei/) to various agencies of the government and use it for legitimate purposes. As of March 31, 2022, the platform has recorded 17,648 pieces of information. Take the information on the fixed-point scooter provided by the Public Transport Office of the Transportation Bureau as an example; it has been downloaded and used more than 42 million times.7. Continue to promote the work related to participatory budgeting. In addition to regularly holding proposal seminars, residents' meetings, proposal review workshops and voting of proposal in each district office, the City also strengthens cooperation with academia. Under the framework of the Partnership between Taipei City Government and Educational Institutions on Planning Participatory Budgeting, they analyze the relevant information in the past 6 years and use it as the basis for the improvement of participatory budgeting.

question_name: Report your jurisdiction's most significant examples of collaboration with government, business, and/or civil society on climate-related issues.
response_answer: 1. Reporting and contacting mechanisms for auditing pollutions by New Taipei City and Taipei City: For cross-jurisdictional cases, the Department of Environmental Protection and the New Taipei City Department of Environmental Protection has established a joint contacting mechanism for prohibiting pollution since 2016. It is handled according to the “Operational Principles for Contacting Mechanisms for Auditing Pollutions by New Taipei City and Taipei City.” If cross-regional pollution is found, a 24-hour reporting window and Line contact group of the Government’s environmental inspection division service center will initiate a joint inspection by the New Taipei City and Taipei City.2. Discharge limits for ammonia nitrogen in the discharge water for public sewage plants are required: in September 2021, the "Water Pollution Prevention and Control License" of Neihu and Dihua Sewage Treatment Plants will tighten the ammonia nitrogen control standards, and the discharging concentration limits of ammonia nitrogen will be tightened to 5mg/L and 6.3mg/L according to the conditions of each plant. When the discharging concentration of ammonia nitrogen at the Neihu and Dihua Sewage Treatment Plant exceeds the concentration limit, the sewage treatment plant is required to submit an improvement report to strengthen the management and control of the quality of ammonia nitrogen discharged.3. Automatic and continuous monitoring of discharged water from public sewage treatment plants: to strengthen the management and monitoring mechanism of public sewage treatment plants, the city's Neihu and Dihua sewage treatment plants are urged to complete automatic and continuous monitoring facilities for discharged water before 2018. Real-time monitoring includes water volume, water temperature, pH, electrical conductivity, and chemical oxygen demand, suspended solids, ammonia nitrogen, and other items. The monitoring of the quality of the water discharged by the public sewage treatment plants is strengthened.4. Create an automatic monitoring network for the quality of the river water: The automatic water quality monitoring stations were established at 4 places, including the Chengde Bridge, Chengmei Changshou Bridge on the Keelung River in 2018, Taipei Bridge on the Danshui River, and Rescue Pier of the Zhongzheng Bridge on the Xindian River in 2020. We expect to complete another one on Jingmei River to build a river water quality monitoring network in 2022. The real-time monitoring includes water temperature, pH, electrical conductivity, dissolved oxygen, suspended solids, ammonia nitrogen, and other items. The quality of the river water will be monitored around the clock.5. Establish a warning mechanism for low dissolved oxygen in rivers: Through the automatic monitoring network of the river water quality, when the dissolved oxygen in the river is low (less than 0.3mg/L for 5 consecutive hours and 2 consecutive days), the inter-agencies warning mechanism will be activated. This includes the department of Environmental Protection's cleaning team strengthening river inspections, the interception station of the Public Works Department strengthening the interception of sewage on sunny days, proper operation of public sewage treatment plants, and the Water Resources Department of the Public Works Bureau preparing sewage removing vessels to remove the energies to prevent fish from dying.

response_answer: To enhance the community's disaster prevention awareness and disaster prevention and protection capabilities, one village in each of the 12 administrative districts in the City is selected to promote resilient community work. The major promotion processes are enlightenment, initiation, conducting environment surveys, discussing countermeasures for disaster prevention and protection, establishing organizations and formulating projects, disaster prevention and rescue training, community observation and visits, and conducting emergency drills. From 2021 to the end of March 2022, a total of 15 relevant education and training were conducted, with 630 participants and 7 actual military exercises and military stimulations, with 255 participants. We effectively integrated disaster prevention and rescue organizations, strengthen task forces, mechanisms for handling disaster prevention and protection, and various emergency equipment in the villages to enable them to be equipped with certain self-help and mutual cooperation capabilities.In 2019, the “Taipei City Promotion Taskforce of Flood Resilient-Resistant Community Project” was initiated. A professional consultant team was entrusted to handle the advocacy and the promotion of disaster-resistant matters in the communities and on campuses. In 2019, we promoted communities located in the Dahu Village in Neihu District, Jiangshan Village in Zhongshan District, and Guangneng Village in Datong District. In 2020, we promoted the Zhonghua Village in Songshan District, Heping Village in Wanhua District, and Yide Village in Beitou District as disaster prevention demonstration communities. In 2021, we promoted Qunxian Village in Daan District, Jiying Village in Zhongshan District, and Xingwang Village in Wenshan District as disaster prevention demonstration communities.This project uses Opendata, such as flood simulation maps, flood protection plans, and rain gauges, and promotes the flood resilient disaster-resistance community project, so that community residents have the ability to respond to disasters and emergencies. Community courses on disaster prevention include at least the “composition of the disaster prevention community work team and guidance meeting,” “enlightenment and initiation of disaster prevention community,” “community diagnosis for disasters in the environment and formulation of countermeasures for issues on disaster prevention and protection,” “establishment of community disaster prevention and protection organization, task division and operation,” “community disaster prevention and protection, rescue training or seminars,” “disaster prevention personnel training and counseling,” and community emergency drills are conducted. When heavy rain is forecasted, pre-disaster preparations are carried out. When the heavy rain occurs, residents are quickly gathered for evacuation, rescue, and other emergency responses, and after the heavy rain stops, post-disaster recovery is carried out, such as cutting down the collapsed trees on the road, assisting the evacuation of disadvantaged groups, CPR and AED performance, flood gate operations, and water pump operations.In addition, Taipei City Government Hydraulic Engineering Office of the Public Works Department also refers to the analysis of flooding potential and the water accumulation events over the years before the flood period every year. For urban areas with relatively lowland and high risk of water accumulation (102 areas in 2021), mechanical water pumps are leased in advance during the typhoon and heavy rain period to reduce risks and occurrence of disasters.

response_answer: In 2015, the Environmental Protection Administration of Taiwan established the "Greenhouse Gas Offset Project Management Regulations" to encourage the reduction of emissions, and to grant reduction credits (carbon rights) after verification and review by a third party. With reference to the United Nations Clean Development Mechanism (CDM), a new category of "micro-scale offset projects" was added in 2018 to encourage small and medium-sized enterprises and other small emission sources, and to expand the participation of the transportation and residential and commercial sectors to promote the development of emission reduction technologies for all types of sources.Taipei City and Taipei 101 are working together to reduce carbon emissions, and this is the first example of micro-scale offset for the residential and commercial sector in Taiwan. The City assisted Taipei 101 in replacing the lighting in the underground parking lot of the commercial office building in 2020, and upgrading 2,841 T5 fluorescent lighting fixtures to high-efficiency LED lighting fixtures. It is estimated that the reduction of electricity consumption by 510,000 kWh per year will result in a total of 2,718 tons of carbon reduction in 10 years, and each side will receive 50% of the carbon rights, and 92 tons of carbon rights were obtained in 2021. In 2021, the City actively assisted the Carrefour Chongqing Store in taking stock of the efficiency of its air-conditioning equipment, and proposed a project to replace its high-efficiency magnetic floating ice and water machine, saving an average of 343,000 kWh of electricity per year. It is the first case in the country where a large retailer completed a micro-scale offset.The City will continue to work with businesses to promote the micro-scale offset program, leading more large corporate customers to follow through and move toward a net zero future.

column_name: Describe the impacts on vulnerable populations and sectors^
response_answer: 1. The temperature in Taipei City may likely soar given the rapid economic development, dense population, dense-graded pavement and dense buildings, and its basin formation. Since 2018, the Central Weather Bureau issued forecasts and warnings to define extremely high temperature, and compared to the 20th century, the average number of days of extreme high temperature in Taipei City has increased by about 20 days per year. There were 66 days when the temperature is more than 36°C in Taipei City in 2020, of which there were 13 days when the temperature is over 38°C. The weather station even recorded temperature as high as 39.7°C on July 24  2020, which hit the 124-year record. According to the scenario of higher greenhouse gas emissions (RCP8.5) announced by the National Science and Technology Center for Disaster Reduction (NCDR), the temperature in Taipei was more than 36°C for about 20 days per year in the early 21st century and may reach up to 100 days per year by the end of the 21st century. In the future, the number of days of extreme high temperature may occur more frequently and seriously affect the power supply facilities and health of citizens in Taipei City.2. Extreme hot weather will lead to the breeding of vectors and cause yellow fever mosquito and other vector mosquitoes to spread northward, which will expand the scope of dengue fever, and citizens will face health risks. The resulting heat wave also increases outdoor workers, such as construction workers’ risks of heat injuries, heat stroke, and dermopathy among outdoor workers. It also increases the severity of heat injury symptoms for infants, the elderly, and low-income households who cannot afford air conditioning and electricity.3. The main impacts of extreme hot days include increased electricity consumption, and health and hygiene issues, such as increased demand for air-conditioning, resulting in an increase in electrical load. The waste heat from air-conditioning results in the repetition of the heat island effect, increasing the burden on the power supply of the energy department. In addition, if there is an overconsumption of electricity and there are no power conditioner, power outages may easily occur, affecting the stable power supply of the commercial and service industries of the city's major economic artery.

question_name: Provide details of your emissions reduction target(s). Please report both long-term and mid-term targets, if applicable.
response_answer: Referring to the net zero emission pathways announced by the International Energy Agency (IEA), advanced countries and international cities, and taking into account the City's population, social, and economic conditions, Taipei City estimates that under the CO2 emission business as usual (BAU) scenario, the City will need to reduce its emissions by 12.26 million metric tons of CO2e in 2050 in order to achieve net zero emissions.The main pathways to achieve net zero emissions in the City are smart and zero-carbon buildings, green transportation, low-carbon transportation, and total recycling and zero waste, as well as strengthening the maintenance and upgrading of carbon sinks, introducing new technologies such as zero-carbon and negative-carbon with the times, and adjusting the corrective pathways on a rolling basis, together with the central government's policies of expanding renewable energy, introducing hydrogen/new energy, reducing the carbon emission coefficient of electricity year by year, and stopping the sale of new fuel vehicles for the City to smoothly transform into a zero-carbon city. The City's 2050 net zero-carbon emission pathway driving direction is outlined below:1. Smart and zero-carbon buildings:In the BAU scenario, it is estimated that the City's residential and commercial sector will emit about 9.69 million metric tons of CO2e by 2050, accounting for 79% of the total carbon emissions. Therefore, it is necessary to promote smart and zero-carbon buildings to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from residential and commercial activities in buildings. The City's approach to promoting smart and zero-carbon buildings is to combine building energy efficiency management with building energy efficiency and the use of renewable/new energy sources to minimize greenhouse gas emissions. On the basis of 2030, existing buildings will be required to conduct energy efficiency inventories and label disclosure in 2040, and public buildings will continue to be renovated at an annual rate of 3% of the total floor area to achieve net zero emission standards. In 2050, all buildings, except general buildings, will be required to meet Class 1+ energy efficiency, and new/commercial/public buildings will be required to use at least 55% renewable energy or hydrogen energy .2. Green transportation and low-carbon transportationIn the BAU scenario, the transportation sector will emit about 2.22 million metric tons of CO2e in 2050, accounting for about 18% of the total carbon emissions. The green transportation and low-carbon transportation pathway is mainly to expand the public transportation network, encourage the use of green transportation, build a friendly environment for the use of green transportation, match the central government's 2040 electric vehicle market share of 100%, and significantly introduce electric vehicles/hydrogen energy vehicles as the main direction. On the basis of 70% green transportation in 2030, the proportion of green transportation is planned to increase to 75% in 2040 and 80% in 2050. The total length of public bicycle lanes will be 596 km with 16,000 bicycles in 2040 and 21,500 in 2050. Continue to promote the sharing of vehicles, with 25,850 by 2040 and 27,500 by 2050. To expand the use of green vehicles, low-carbon transportation zones will be designated as a priority for major trunk roads or bus routes starting in 2040, and will be expanded to the entire city in 2050 to control access for high-carbon vehicles. It is expected that 50% of privately owned vehicles will be electrified by 2040 and 95% by 2050.3. Total recycling and zero wasteIn the BAU scenario, it is estimated that the waste sector will emit 120,000 tons of CO2e greenhouse gases in 2050, accounting for about 1% of the total emissions. In July 2000, the City was the first in the country to implement the per bag trash collection fee, which has effectively promoted the reduction of household garbage by two-thirds at the source and significantly increased the resource recovery rate. On this basis to promote resource recycling and reuse, with the resource recovery rate expected to increase from 70% in 2030 to 75% in 2040 and 80% in 2050. We plan to reach 98% of the sewage treatment population in 2050.In addition to gradually transforming incinerators into high-efficiency green energy power plants to increase power generation, the corresponding treatment facilities for food organic waste, incineration bottom ash, fly ash, and resource waste will be built and integrated into a "total recycling and zero waste" green energy recycling park, so that waste can be converted into renewable energy and renewable materials and recycled. After 2040, the City will start to introduce carbon capture utilize and storage [CCU(S)] and other negative-carbon technologies to gradually reduce carbon emissions from waste and sewage treatment processes and achieve the goal of 2050 net zero emissions in the waste sector.

column_name: Describe how climate-related issues have impacted your jurisdiction's master/development planning
response_answer: The impact of climate change on Taipei City can be divided into mitigation and adaptation in the overall development plan.1. Reduction strategies:The City has set a clear goal of reducing greenhouse gas emissions and will achieve net-zero emissions by 2050. Urban transformation is important during the process of achievement. This issue has expanded beyond environmental protection to industry and energy transition, and from the city’s perspective, it will have a significant effect on Taiwan’s future international competitiveness. From energy, society, industry, economy, livelihood, and other aspects, a more active transformation strategy is required. Therefore, with Agenda 2030 as a foundation, the City will cooperate with the government's energy transition efforts to gradually achieve net-zero emissions by 2050.(1) We plan to promote the development of new buildings with zero-carbons and introduce the building energy history system and smart green building designs to achieve the goal of zero-carbon buildings and a circular economy by 2050.(2) Taipei City actively expands the development and use of renewable energy. The City has launched the "Taipei Chase the Sun Project" and proposed 4 major directions (tenders for municipal properties, subsidies for private installation, promotion of smart grids, and establish power plants run jointly by the public and private sectors). These measures allow the City to use its limited space to create a circular, low-carbon green capital and drive productions and employment opportunities in solar-related industries.(3) Promote the optimization of bus routes, full electrification of buses, transfer discounts, and transit passes for public transportation. The goal is to increase the ratio of green transportation from 60% to 80% by 2050.2. Adaptation strategy:As Taipei City is a basin, it may easily cause a heat island effect due to high temperature, and instantaneous heavy rainfall is also likely to cause flooding with drainage failures. For this high vulnerability project, the City has prepared a comprehensive adaptation plan, including:(1) A high-temperature warning system has been established. Measures such as sprinkling watering on the roads, labor inspections for outdoor workers, and care for the elderly that live alone have been initiated to cope with the high risks of extreme heat to the disadvantaged groups.(2) Promote sponge city policies, adopt measures such as permeable pavement in parks and squares, set up green spaces and parks, and rainwater harvesting to increase the capability of urban flood detention and to cope with climate risks such as typhoons and heavy rainfall.(3) Formulate Garden City policies, actively encourage the use of urban vacant land, city-owned and private building roofs, or pastoral bases of private enterprises. By increasing the green coverage ratio and extending and supporting the green space system, the city’s ecological function is enhanced.

response_answer: The Taipei City Government has formulated/promoted the following plans: Taipei City’s disaster prevention and protection, strengthening plan, Taipei City's post-disaster recovery and reconstruction program, flood disaster-resistant community project 1. Disaster Prevention and Protection Strengthening Project - resilient communitiesTo enhance the community's disaster prevention awareness and disaster prevention and protection capabilities, one village in each of the 12 administrative districts in the City is selected to promote resilient community work. The major promotion processes are enlightening, initiation, conducting environment surveys, discussing countermeasures for disaster prevention and protection, establishing organizations and formulating projects, disaster prevention and rescue training, community observation and visits, and conducting emergency drills. 2. Enhance Taipei City's post-disaster recovery operationsIn order to effectively implement the post-disaster recovery to ensure the safety of the citizen’s lives, their properties, and the sustainable development of the city, the City has formulated post-disaster recovery plans and standard operating procedures, necessary financial measures for post-disaster reconstruction,  living arrangements for disaster victims, reconstruction of basic and public facilities, post-disaster environmental recovery, industrial restoration and psychological treatment and life rehabilitation for disaster victims.3. Flood disaster-resistant community projectTaipei City Government Hydraulic Engineering Office of the Public Works Department promotes the “Flood Disaster-resistant Community Project,” using non-structural means to improve the city's flood resistance.In 2019, the “Taipei City Promotion Taskforce of Flood Resilient-Resistant Community Project” was initiated.  In 2021, we promoted 3 Districts as disaster prevention demonstration communities.This project uses Open data and promotes the flood resilient disaster-resistance community project, so that community residents could respond to disasters and emergencies. When heavy rain is forecasted, pre-disaster preparations are carried out. When the heavy rain occurs, residents are quickly gathered for evacuation, rescue, and other emergency responses, and after the heavy rain stops, post-disaster recovery is carried out.

response_answer: The Gujarat SAPCC (2021) includes climate projections from three RCP scenarios, RCP 2.6, RCP 4.5 and RCP 8.5, which reflect high, medium and low efforts to curb emissions, respectively. These scenarios are modelled for short term (2011 to 2040), midterm (2041 to 2070) and long term (2071 to 2100) periods. Given that the target year for the Net Zero Climate Resilient City Action Plan for Ahmedabad is 2070, climate scenarios for the short term and midterm are considered for further analysis. Details of climate projections derived from SAPCC (Gujarat 2021) are shown in Annexure 4.1 and reflected in section 4.2.2.1. Please refer Annexures_ Ahmedabad Climate Resilient City Action Plan_Towards A Net Zero Future 2070.

response_answer: Refer Chapter 6  on Scenario Planning for Future Emissions Reduction (page no. 173 to 185) and Chapter 7 on Ahmedabad's Goals and Strategies for Climate Resilience (page no. 186 to 311) of Ahmedabad Climate Resilient City Action Plan - Towards A Net Zero Future by 2070.  This action plan identifies GHG mitigation targets for 2030 (short term targets), 2050 (intermediate targets) and 2070 (Net Zero Target).Ahmedabad’s Net Zero CRCAP aims to make the city climate-resilient and advance towards net zero emissions by 2070. It proposes strategies such as promoting energy efficiency in buildings, increasing RE use, adopting sustainable waste management practices, and encouraging low-carbon transport options. Ahmedabad’s Climate Resilient City Action Plan (CRCAP) – Towards Net Zero by 2070 has been developed using the Net Zero ClimateResilientCITIES methodology. This includes guidance for baseline analyses and identification, and prioritization of climate resilient strategies and targets.Scenario Planning, a critical step in the process of developing an ambitious climate action plan, establishes the business as usual (BAU) future emissions trajectory. Emissions reduction strategies, scales of action and multiple targets are defined and analysed to arrive at two  distinct emissions reduction pathways; the Progressive Action Scenario and the Net Zero Emissions Pathway.BAU Projection: The BAU projection shows the level of GHG emissions that would result in the future if the current levels and patterns of climate action are followed. It assumes that no additional emissions reduction efforts and measures will be undertaken, beyond those already in place. The BAU projection represents the ‘baseline condition’ and serves as a reference point for assessing the impact of emissions reduction scenarios or pathways.Progressive Action Scenario: The Progressive Action scenario represents the level of GHG emissions resulting from increased levels of climate action being implemented at the city-scale as compared to the BAU scenario. It considers the goals and guidelines of national and state government policies and programs, while being defined by and reflective of on-ground scenarios. Factors such as local conditions, current urban infrastructure and service provision, level of adoption of climate solutions, resources, and capacities are considered while determining the targets and actions proposed.Net Zero Pathway: The Net Zero Pathway is based on the commitment of GoI to achieve net zero emissions by 2070. It is defined by ambitious climate actions and efforts that are required for the city to transition towards meeting net zero GHG targets by 2070. The actions in this pathway build on the targets set by the national and state government through various plans, policies, and programs to realize this goal.Guiding Principles for estimating the BAU scenario:1. The relationship between the quantum of emissions and the rate of urbanization is assumed to be directly proportional. 2. Urbanization rate is influenced by the population and economic growth, which are affected by interdependent factors such as secondary and tertiary sector growth, education levels, birth and death rates, life expectancy, and migration.3. Urbanization refers to expanding urban centres in terms of geographical area and population, driven by shifts in the economy from primary to secondary, tertiary, or quaternary activities.4. For modelling of the projected BAU emissions, three different urbanization pathways have been evaluated based on the UN’s World Urbanisation Prospects methodologies, the IPCC-endorsed Shared Socio-economic Pathways, and guidance from the Global Cities Institute. These pathways represent three different urbanization rates: rapid, moderate, and slow.5. The rapid urbanization pathway assumes the highest population and economic growth rates, while the slow urbanization scenario assumes the lowest rates. The moderate urbanization scenario falls between these two extremes.6. Urbanisation patterns are dependent on government policies that can either promote or hinder urbanisation rate. Therefore, for a city undertaking emissions modelling and scenario planning, the choice of applying a particular urbanization rate and corresponding population growth rates ultimately rests with the city and state governments. The CRCAP for Ahmedabad adopts the moderate urbanization scenario.

response_answer: Ahmedabad Climate Resilient City Action Plan (Towards A Net Zero Future by 2070) is prepared through intense stakeholder consultation  and launched by the city in June 2023.  This action plan includes GPC compliant GHG emissions inventory, ward and area level vulnerability and risk assessment, scenario planning based on various National and State Government targets. City is considering  sector wise climate change mitigation and adaptation interventions/ actions/ projects  during Annual Municipal Budget Planning every year, which is being approved by city council (Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation General Board).  City has constituted Climate Core Team, chaired by Municipal Commissioner and  includes head of various departments. Climate Core Team meets every quarter to discuss climate resilient interventions and monitoring implementation status. Information and updates from Climate Core Team is being used for Annual Municipal Budget planning every year.  Please refer below sections from Ahmedabad Climate Resilient City Action Plan (Towards A Net Zero Future).1) Annexure 1 (Page A2 to A6) for information on Stakeholder Committee and Climate Core team ; 2) Chapter 3 (section 3.1.5, 3.2.7, 3.3.2, 3.4.11, 3.5.6, 3.6.2) for information on sector wise budgetary planning for climate actions in FY 2023-24.

question_name: Provide details on the most significant climate hazards faced by your jurisdiction.
column_name: Describe the impacts on vulnerable populations and sectors^
response_answer: Rise in extreme rainfall events and insufficient stormwater drainage leads to urban flooding. Vulnerable populations, such as the urban poor, are the most impacted due to poor living conditions and limited resources. The flood risk is assessed by analysing rainfall trends, spatial analysis of waterlogged areas, and ward-level analysis of water-borne diseases, revealing areas most affected by flooding. Issues such as heavy siltation in stormwater drains and improper waste and sewage disposal exacerbate flooding, impacting health, mobility, and economic productivity.Some of the areas severely affected by waterlogging include Naranpura, India Colony, Indrapuri, Khokhra, Thakkarbapa Nagar, Isanpur, Bodakdev, Paldi, Maninagar, Vasna, S P Stadium, Saraspur, and Vatva. The city is experiencing a rise in urban flooding hazards due to intense rainfall occurrences. Residents within a 250 m radius of 166 waterlogged areas or flood points face elevated risks and are susceptible to severe health hazards.Population Groups Vulnerable to Urban Flooding: Children, elderly, women, and those with special needs are most impacted by urban flooding. Limited access to health facilities, emergency services, and urban services during floods mainly affect these groups. They also suffer from a lack of inclusive infrastructure and access to information. Urban poor living in compromised housing conditions and with limited access to health centres are susceptible to disease outbreaks. Approximately Approximately, 4.3% of the city’s total area and 9.5% of the city’s population i.e., 0.7 million (0.3 million females, 0.4 million males – including 55,000 children; 34,000 elders; 20,000 people with special needs; 0.2 million illiterate people) is vulnerable to urban flooding. Vulnerable population by income group includes 88,000 people living in slums and 5,000 street side vendors. Urban flooding renders public infrastructure, such as roads, inaccessible; impacting the daily livelihood of street side vendors and slum dwellers. Refer section 4.3.2 (pg.no.116 to123) in attached Ahmedabad Climate Resilient City Action Plan (Towards A Net Zero Future).

reporting_authority: C40; CDP Cities; ICLEI - Local Governments for Sustainability; Race to Zero; Global Covenant of Mayors
question_name: Provide details on your climate risk and vulnerability assessment.
response_answer: According to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), risks of climate-related impacts result from the interaction of climate related hazards, vulnerability, and exposure of human and natural systems. Climate Risk and Vulnerability Assessment for Ahmedabad includes the analysis of risks and vulnerability of urban systems and population of Ahmedabad city due to climate hazards and air pollution. This baseline assessment supported city to adopt climate sensitive urban planning, effectively manage climate change induced risks, and efficiently implement climate resilient policies and interventions.The Climate Risk and Vulnerability Assessment (CRVA) follows ICLEI South Asia’s ‘Towards Net Zero ClimateResilientCITIES’ methodology. Climate Risk and Vulnerability Assessment for Ahmedabad is divided into three parts that address; i) analysis of climate trends and projection scenario, ii) assessment and prioritization of hazards and risks based on likelihood and consequences, and iii) vulnerability assessment. Inputs from the climate core team and the stakeholder committee of AMC, captured through Shared Learning Dialogues (SLDs), are considered in the assessment.Step 1: Climate Trends and ProjectionsHistoric climate and weather data from 1970 to 2020 was analysed to understand trends and patterns of change in temperature and rainfall. Climate projections for Representative Concentration Pathways (RCPs) till 2070, were derived from the State Action Plan on ClimateChange (SAPCC), Gujarat 2021. This information was substantiated with inputs from expertsduring stakeholder consultations. Based on the trend analysis and future projections, climate scenario statements were developed.Step 2: Risk AssessmentBased on climate trends and projections, climate risks were identified and analysed according to the likelihood of occurrence and consequence. Inferences drawn from GIS based spatial analysis and analysis of relevant climate and qualitative information received during stakeholder consultations, informed the climate risk assessment. Information from the State Disaster Management Plan (Gujarat 2016-17) and District Disaster Management Plan (Ahmedabad 2021)corroborated the results. It was observed that the city of Ahmedabad is vulnerable to extremeheat, urban floods, and air pollution. Vulnerable urban systems due to extreme heat, urban flood and air pollution were assessed. Step 3: Vulnerability AssessmentResults from the risk assessment, along with data received from various departments of AMC, and qualitative information received during stakeholder consultations and one to one meetings, were used to assess the vulnerability of urban systems and their impact on people.  The impacts on vulnerable groups such as low-income populations (focusing on hawkers, street side vendors, and slum dwellers), women, children, people with disabilities and the uneducated were also assessed. Vulnerable areas were identified following spatial analysis - Maps reflecting this analysis are included. The impacts of climate risks and air pollution on basic urban services (water, wastewater, stormwater, solid waste management, transport, urban greens) and emergency services (hospitals and fire services) were examined. Ward wise complaints, by urban sector and complaint types, from AMC’s Comprehensive Complaints Redressal System (CCRS), were spatially analysed; this information supported the identification of areas that are vulnerable to fragile urban systems. For each urban system, the populations that are most vulnerable are also identified and their adaptive capacity is assessed in terms of their access to resources, access to information and their capacity to respond to stresses. Hotspot areas or highly vulnerable wards were identified through a map overlay technique, wherein geospatial information on complaints, climate risks/hazards and gaps in urban infrastructure and/or services were superimposed and analysed. Details and inferences of the climate vulnerability assessment are included in section 4.3 of attached Ahmedabad Climate Resilient City Action Plan .Please refer Chapter 4 from page number 97 to 151 from attached Ahmedabad Climate Resilient City Action Plan (Towards A Net Zero Future).

question_name: Provide details of your emissions reduction target(s). Please report both long-term and mid-term targets, if applicable.
response_answer: Refer Chapter 6  on Scenario Planning for Future Emissions Reduction (page no. 173 to 185) and Chapter 7 on Ahmedabad's Goals and Strategies for Climate Resilience (page no. 186 to 311) of Ahmedabad Climate Resilient City Action Plan - Towards A Net Zero Future by 2070.  This action plan identifies GHG mitigation targets for 2030 (short term targets), 2050 (intermediate targets) and 2070 (Net Zero Target).Ahmedabad’s Net Zero CRCAP aims to make the city climate-resilient and advance towards net zero emissions by 2070. It proposes strategies such as promoting energy efficiency in buildings, increasing RE use, adopting sustainable waste management practices, and encouraging low-carbon transport options. Ahmedabad’s Climate Resilient City Action Plan (CRCAP) – Towards Net Zero by 2070 has been developed using the Net Zero ClimateResilientCITIES methodology. This includes guidance for baseline analyses and identification, and prioritization of climate resilient strategies and targets.Scenario Planning, a critical step in the process of developing an ambitious climate action plan, establishes the business as usual (BAU) future emissions trajectory. Emissions reduction strategies, scales of action and multiple targets are defined and analysed to arrive at two  distinct emissions reduction pathways; the Progressive Action Scenario and the Net Zero Emissions Pathway.BAU Projection: The BAU projection shows the level of GHG emissions that would result in the future if the current levels and patterns of climate action are followed. It assumes that no additional emissions reduction efforts and measures will be undertaken, beyond those already in place. The BAU projection represents the ‘baseline condition’ and serves as a reference point for assessing the impact of emissions reduction scenarios or pathways.Progressive Action Scenario: The Progressive Action scenario represents the level of GHG emissions resulting from increased levels of climate action being implemented at the city-scale as compared to the BAU scenario. It considers the goals and guidelines of national and state government policies and programs, while being defined by and reflective of on-ground scenarios. Factors such as local conditions, current urban infrastructure and service provision, level of adoption of climate solutions, resources, and capacities are considered while determining the targets and actions proposed.Net Zero Pathway: The Net Zero Pathway is based on the commitment of GoI to achieve net zero emissions by 2070. It is defined by ambitious climate actions and efforts that are required for the city to transition towards meeting net zero GHG targets by 2070. The actions in this pathway build on the targets set by the national and state government through various plans, policies, and programs to realize this goal.Guiding Principles for estimating the BAU scenario:1. The relationship between the quantum of emissions and the rate of urbanization is assumed to be directly proportional. 2. Urbanization rate is influenced by the population and economic growth, which are affected by interdependent factors such as secondary and tertiary sector growth, education levels, birth and death rates, life expectancy, and migration.3. Urbanization refers to expanding urban centres in terms of geographical area and population, driven by shifts in the economy from primary to secondary, tertiary, or quaternary activities.4. For modelling of the projected BAU emissions, three different urbanization pathways have been evaluated based on the UN’s World Urbanisation Prospects methodologies, the IPCC-endorsed Shared Socio-economic Pathways, and guidance from the Global Cities Institute. These pathways represent three different urbanization rates: rapid, moderate, and slow.5. The rapid urbanization pathway assumes the highest population and economic growth rates, while the slow urbanization scenario assumes the lowest rates. The moderate urbanization scenario falls between these two extremes.6. Urbanisation patterns are dependent on government policies that can either promote or hinder urbanisation rate. Therefore, for a city undertaking emissions modelling and scenario planning, the choice of applying a particular urbanization rate and corresponding population growth rates ultimately rests with the city and state governments. The CRCAP for Ahmedabad adopts the moderate urbanization scenario.

column_name: Describe the impacts on vulnerable populations and sectors^
response_answer: Air Pollution: Air pollution risk is assessed by examining trends of primary air pollutants, spatial analysis of pollution in the city, and incidence of acute respiratory illness (ARI). The most concerning pollutants are PM10 and PM2.5, with the latter posing a significant health risk. High PM10 concentration (almost double the standard of 60 μg/m3) and high PM2.5 concentration (more than 40 μg/m3) may severely impact the health of people. Exceedances are observed on 52% of all monitored days.Areas with high PM10 concentration include Raikhad, Maninagar, Narol, Vatva GIDC, Sola, and Naroda, while regions with high PM2.5 concentration include Pirana, Raikhad, Bopal, S P Stadium, Vatva GIDC, and Airport. The increase in air pollution can severely impact health, especially for those with co-morbid conditions. Ahmedabad recorded 2,037 air-borne disease cases (852 ARI and 1,185 tuberculosis) during 2021-22.Urban Areas Vulnerable to Air Pollution: Areas most impacted by high PM10 and PM2.5 concentrations and also record an increased number of airborne disease cases include Jamalpur, Danilimda, Maninagar, Baherampura, Lambha, and Vatva GIDC. In total, 55.3% of the city area is at high risk due to air pollution, affecting 39.5% of the total city population i.e., 2.8 million people (1.3 million females and 1.5 million males, including 0.2 million children; 0.1 million elders; 85,000 people with special needs; 0.6 million illiterate people) is vulnerable to air pollution. Vulnerable population by income group includes 0.4 million people living in slums and 23,000 street side vendors. Urban flooding renders public infrastructure, such as roads, inaccessible; impacting the daily livelihood of street side vendors and slum dwellers. Refer section 4.3.3 (pg.no.124 to129) in attached Ahmedabad Climate Resilient City Action Plan (Towards A Net Zero Future).

column_name: Describe how climate-related issues have impacted your jurisdiction's financial planning
response_answer: Based on Ahmedabad Climate Resilient City Action Plan (Towards A Net Zero Future by 2070) and climate related issues, city has proposed various climate resilient interventions, which has increased capital allocation of Annual Municipal Budget (i.e., lake interlinking, replacing old water supply and sewerage network, 7MW of RE plants, developing urban forests to increase in green cover, biomining of legacy waste etc.). By implementing climate resilient interventions (i.e., 21MW of RE installed for municipal facilities, replacement of streetlights with EE LED lights) has reduced the operating costs and increased revenue. Also, city has proposed some of the projects based on PPP model for accessing climate finance (i.e., 2000 TPD waste to energy plant, 500 TPD waste to bio-CNG plant etc.). City is in progress for releasing Green Bonds under Government of India's AMRUT 2.0 Scheme. City is also part of Gujarat Resilient Cities Program (GRCP), where city is receiving INR 30,000 million from the World Bank for climate resilient infrastructure for wastewater sector.  Please refer below sections from Ahmedabad Climate Resilient City Action Plan (Towards A Net Zero Future).1) Chapter 3 (section 3.1.5, 3.2.7, 3.3.2, 3.4.11, 3.5.6, 3.6.2) for information on sector wise budgetary planning for climate actions in FY 2023-24.

question_name: Report details on the climate action plan or strategy that addresses mitigation, adaptation (resilience), and/or energy-related issues in your jurisdiction.
response_answer: AMC used the ‘Net Zero ClimateResilientCITIES’ methodology to develop its climate action plan to achieve net zero emissions by 2070. This methodology includes a multi-stakeholder approach that involves assessing climate vulnerabilities, estimating GHG emissions, proposing climate resilient interventions that address adaptation and mitigation, and developing frameworks for financing, implementing, monitoring and reporting climate actions. By incorporating expertise and experience from initiatives led by ICLEI – Local Governments for Sustainability, the plan benefits from a wealth of knowledge and best practices in climate planning and action. This methodology provided a step-wise approach to address climate change adaptation and mitigation. Its nine steps are organised into three phases: Analyse, Act, and Accelerate. Ahmedabad embarked on a climate-resilient journey through this ninestep process. AMC committed to climate action by forming a City Climate Core Team to lead the charge. A Stakeholder Committee was constituted to seek inputs from and involve the community, including the private sector, in the implementation of the action plan. The city’s socio-environmental landscape and key challenges were identified, climate risks and vulnerability assessed, and emissions baselines established. Goals, strategies, and actions that address identified climate vulnerabilities and thematic actions to reduce GHG emissions across sectors, were defined. To guide emissions reduction strategies across three different planning horizons, i.e., 2030, 2050 and 2070, the CRCAP scales the defined goals, strategies, and actions across two emissions reduction scenarios.

question_name: Provide details on the most significant climate hazards faced by your jurisdiction.
column_name: Describe the impacts on vulnerable populations and sectors^
response_answer: The assessment involved analysing indicators like air temperature trends and future scenarios, land surface temperature (LST), heat index analysis, and heat wave trends. Air temperature trends were studied using IMD data. LST was assessed using satellite imagery. Heat index and heat wave trends were analysed using AMC data. The LST Analysis varies depending on land use, infrastructure, and human activities. It varies between 29°C to 47°C during day and 26°C to 29°C during night, indicating potential hotspots.Heat Index Analysis (feels-like temperature) is a combination of air temperature and humidity. It was plotted, indicating potential risk areas with a ‘feels-like’ temperature of more than 43°C. The analysis revealed an increasing trend year on year.Ahmedabad has seen increased heat wave events with significant health impacts. A correlation exists between heat wave events and heatstroke-related morbidity and mortality.The city’s most vulnerable areas are those with high LST and ‘feels-like’ temperature. Such areas include wards like Amraiwadi, Bapunagar, Viratnagar, and industrial areas. Extreme heat may impact water and energy demand. As per Gujarat SAPCC, the number of heat wave events has increased by 4 events from 1951 to 2019 and is expected to increase by 5-30 events by 2070. This increase in heat wave events may have severe public health implications.Elderly, children, women, differently abled, uneducated, and poor people are most vulnerable to extreme heat conditions. The people especially living in slums have poor living conditions, and limited access to cooling options and healthcare. In Ahmedabad, 5.1 million people (2.4 million females, 2.7 million males) are vulnerable, constituting a significant 72.1% of the total population (including 0.4 million children, 0.3 million elders, 0.2 million people with special needs, 1.1 million illiterate people). Vulnerable population by income group includes 0.7 million people living in slums and 0.45 million street side vendors. Vulnerable population with poor workplace conditions include 770 workers at dumpsites and material recovery facilities (MRF), which are impacted due to accelerated decomposition rates and potentially hazardous conditions in open dumpsites. Refer section 4.3.1 (pg.no.104 to115) in attached Ahmedabad Climate Resilient City Action Plan (Towards A Net Zero Future).

question_name: Provide details of your emissions reduction target(s). Please report both long-term and mid-term targets, if applicable.
response_answer: Refer Chapter 6  on Scenario Planning for Future Emissions Reduction (page no. 173 to 185) and Chapter 7 on Ahmedabad's Goals and Strategies for Climate Resilience (page no. 186 to 311) of Ahmedabad Climate Resilient City Action Plan - Towards A Net Zero Future by 2070.  This action plan identifies GHG mitigation targets for 2030 (short term targets), 2050 (intermediate targets) and 2070 (Net Zero Target).Ahmedabad’s Net Zero CRCAP aims to make the city climate-resilient and advance towards net zero emissions by 2070. It proposes strategies such as promoting energy efficiency in buildings, increasing RE use, adopting sustainable waste management practices, and encouraging low-carbon transport options. Ahmedabad’s Climate Resilient City Action Plan (CRCAP) – Towards Net Zero by 2070 has been developed using the Net Zero ClimateResilientCITIES methodology. This includes guidance for baseline analyses and identification, and prioritization of climate resilient strategies and targets.Scenario Planning, a critical step in the process of developing an ambitious climate action plan, establishes the business as usual (BAU) future emissions trajectory. Emissions reduction strategies, scales of action and multiple targets are defined and analysed to arrive at two  distinct emissions reduction pathways; the Progressive Action Scenario and the Net Zero Emissions Pathway.BAU Projection: The BAU projection shows the level of GHG emissions that would result in the future if the current levels and patterns of climate action are followed. It assumes that no additional emissions reduction efforts and measures will be undertaken, beyond those already in place. The BAU projection represents the ‘baseline condition’ and serves as a reference point for assessing the impact of emissions reduction scenarios or pathways.Progressive Action Scenario: The Progressive Action scenario represents the level of GHG emissions resulting from increased levels of climate action being implemented at the city-scale as compared to the BAU scenario. It considers the goals and guidelines of national and state government policies and programs, while being defined by and reflective of on-ground scenarios. Factors such as local conditions, current urban infrastructure and service provision, level of adoption of climate solutions, resources, and capacities are considered while determining the targets and actions proposed.Net Zero Pathway: The Net Zero Pathway is based on the commitment of GoI to achieve net zero emissions by 2070. It is defined by ambitious climate actions and efforts that are required for the city to transition towards meeting net zero GHG targets by 2070. The actions in this pathway build on the targets set by the national and state government through various plans, policies, and programs to realize this goal.Guiding Principles for estimating the BAU scenario:1. The relationship between the quantum of emissions and the rate of urbanization is assumed to be directly proportional. 2. Urbanization rate is influenced by the population and economic growth, which are affected by interdependent factors such as secondary and tertiary sector growth, education levels, birth and death rates, life expectancy, and migration.3. Urbanization refers to expanding urban centres in terms of geographical area and population, driven by shifts in the economy from primary to secondary, tertiary, or quaternary activities.4. For modelling of the projected BAU emissions, three different urbanization pathways have been evaluated based on the UN’s World Urbanisation Prospects methodologies, the IPCC-endorsed Shared Socio-economic Pathways, and guidance from the Global Cities Institute. These pathways represent three different urbanization rates: rapid, moderate, and slow.5. The rapid urbanization pathway assumes the highest population and economic growth rates, while the slow urbanization scenario assumes the lowest rates. The moderate urbanization scenario falls between these two extremes.6. Urbanisation patterns are dependent on government policies that can either promote or hinder urbanisation rate. Therefore, for a city undertaking emissions modelling and scenario planning, the choice of applying a particular urbanization rate and corresponding population growth rates ultimately rests with the city and state governments. The CRCAP for Ahmedabad adopts the moderate urbanization scenario.

question_name: Report on how climate change impacts health outcomes and health services in your jurisdiction.
response_answer: Accessibility to health care infrastructure is essential to improve living standards and reduce vulnerability to climate and other disasters. Slum dwellers and people with special needs, with limited access to emergency service infrastructure, public transport, and green spaces, are more vulnerable to extreme climate events.Accessibility to health care services has been examined spatially, in line with the Urban and Regional Development Plan Formulation and Implementation (URDPFI) guidelines and the Development Plan of Ahmedabad.Hospitals are marked spatially and correlated with urban flood risk areas to identify critical areas with limited accessibility due to water logging/ urban flood. 651 out of 2,080 hospitals are affected due to urban flood. In areas such as Maninagar, at least 19 hospitals are affected.Ahmedabad has 2,080 hospitals with a capacity of 34,432 beds (5 beds per 1000 persons), exceeding the WHO guideline of 3 beds per 100 persons. Around 99.7% of the population (7.2 million people) has easy access (within 3km distance) to health care facilities. Considering the cost of treatment in private hospitals, accessibility to government health care facilities (including Community Health Centres of AMC), especially for slum dwellers, has been examined separately. Residents of slums in Vatva, Shyamal and Dudeshwar areas need to travel more than 4.5 km to access government hospitals. Slums in these areas are at high risk due to exposure to extreme heat and urban flood risks and limited accessibility to government health care facilities.Population rendered vulnerable due to distant health care facilities: 0.25% of the total population in the city (18,000 people); 20% of all slum dwellers (0.2 million slum population).Further details on accessibility to health care facilities: 94.1% of the total population (6.7 million people) can access health care facilities within 1 km, 4.7% (0.3 million people) within 2 km, and 1% (75,000 people) within 3 km. 25% of all slum dwellers (0.2 million people) can access health care facilities within 1 km, 27% within 2 km, and 27% within 3 km.Refer section 4.3.5.5 (page no. 146) of Ahmedabad Climate Resilient City Action Plan - Towards A Net Zero Future 2070

AMC has targeted to 5000 residential societies.  5) Ahmedabad is developing percolating wells in the city at 8 locations in FY 2023-24. (Locations prioritised by AMC: Ladies Garden behind Rajpath Club, AMC plot at Anandnagar, Ambavadi opposite Kalyan Jewellers, Madhumalti Awas at Kathwada, everest cross road at saraspur, M S Apartment at Trikampura, Shahwadi Municipal School at Lambha, Patel Vaas at Shahwadi)These actions are part of Ahmedabad Climate Resilient City Action Plan (Towards A Net Zero Future), which is attached in previous section.

response_answer: Ahmedabad Development Plan for 2031(prepared in 2021) is emphasizing on 1) densification of existing areas for optimum resource utilization, 2) enhance the skyline through additional FSIs in central business districts, 3) densification along transit corridors through transit-oriented zone (200m on both sides of metro and BRTS transit corridor, eastern high-density corridor between Narol-Naroda highway (NH8) and 132 feet road on eastern side of the city), 5) development of growth centres around the city and providing logistic zones etc. This planning will help Ahmedabad to manage future growth, regulate density and organize land use within the urban area, which will not only help to provide effective and efficient urban services but also conserve natural resources, save energy, and mitigate GHG emissions. Ahmedabad Development Plan for 2031 also emphasizes on blue green infrastructure management and planning, including lake development, open/ green space conservation and management. Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation is following Town Planning Scheme (local area planning concept), which is micro level implementation of larger Development Plan.Please refer below sections from Ahmedabad Climate Resilient City Action Plan (Towards A Net Zero Future).1) Chapter 2 (Section 2.6 - from page number 56 to 60) for land use and development planning
